A question might naturally arise: how then did this Vedic authority reach its current state? The present era speaks of the deities' calculations. However, the calculations of the Vedas and Upanishads speak solely of illumination. Similarly, we have received various revelations over the past sixteen and a half years. Fully comprehending and applying this knowledge will take ages. When utilized according to these revelations, the present-day Trimurti system—namely the Vaishnava, Shakta, and Shaiva traditions of worship—must attain completion through the path of the Guru and the lineage of Manu. It represents an experiential possibility resulting from the integration of the gross, subtle, effect, and cause states for both men and women, young and old alike.
Guruvani
March 1981
Question: Does "experiential possibility" imply that we must harmonize all past events to foster a specific disposition?

Guru: To speak more precisely, there is no need to state that we must foster it. Everything unfolds according to time. Furthermore, it would be more accurate to say that much gets distorted due to our ignorance. The only flaw herein stems from the deficiencies accumulated because we are unable to act appropriately at the right juncture.

Observe the sheer ignorance prevailing in places we herald as progressive. We encounter numerous newspaper reports indicating a significant belief in witchcraft in contemporary times, to the extent that even in America, there is an apprehension of sorcery. Similarly, amidst us who proclaim our culture to be the greatest, what sort of Vedic behaviors are on display? Disgraceful practices, such as inquiring whether one should demonstrate their prowess while in a state of trance, are taking place here.

Even for individuals who feel ashamed to declare "I am a believer," their own families will not permit them to disavow it. Or if they are permitted, the neighbors will end up ostracizing them; such is the situation. Otherwise, the presence of believers mirrors the epidemic of modern politics. Within a single household, one might be a devotee of Vishnu, another of Shiva, a third of Subrahmanya, and a fourth of Kali—each worshipping their chosen deity under the conviction that theirs is supreme. Hearing them speak, we too might feel they are correct. Is it not correct? It is indeed correct. However, this escalates and transforms into the language of the "ego."

In this world, everything that comes into being and perishes, starting from a single grain of sand, possesses its own distinct completeness. One can perceive that this world is sustained by the support of that completeness. Viewed from this perspective, it is evident that even completeness cannot endure without the support of another completeness. We mutually support each other without even comprehending this completeness, thus feeling a sense of grandeur akin to a frog in a well. While navigating life in this world with this understanding, one fundamentally requires something to stand firm upon.

The truth is that if our actions towards it are unified into one, they encompass everything. Otherwise, it will become so void that we will feel entirely incapable of having accomplished anything. Step aside into it for a moment. Then, the recurring anomalies in actions performed at another time for the sake of wholeness will appear as a substantial aggregation. Our current endeavor can merely reduce its magnitude; however, if anyone believes it can be entirely eradicated from this world, such a notion is akin to nihilism.

Therefore, our only recourse is to act while praying for the wisdom to align our spontaneous intellect and capabilities with the divine will, standing closely behind it. For this, the words that convey this divine decree to us serve as our foundation. Upon deep contemplation, we realize that our existential state lacks even the significance of a mere atom. In this atmosphere, if one gazes into this mirage, countless atoms can be observed flickering in and out of existence within the circumference of a single coin. It suffices to consider ourselves merely as one among such atoms. One must not assume a state of absolute nothingness. Doing so would lead to complete voidness.

When it is understood that billions of such atoms mutually interpenetrate and that this penetrative quality pervades everywhere akin to a gas, one should immediately reflect upon whether the nature of our mind is not analogous to this. In such a gaseous state, the mind will completely permeate our desires, exactly like a gas. We must comprehend that this mechanism remains identical, regardless of whether the desire is virtuous or malevolent.

Certain ascetics serve as exemplars of this phenomenon. Placing their faith in the ritualistic nature of particular deities, they elevate and worship them as the Supreme God. Consequently, this transforms into a form of worship dictated by their individual desires. As the number of adherents engaging in this worship multiplies, some develop an inclination to exhibit their prowess. This leads to the urge to exercise mystical powers (*Siddhis*). The application of such powers may be intended to attract crowds or to serve selfish motives. Regardless of the intent, the ultimate objective remains the fulfillment of desire. Moreover, an individual's desire has the potential to inflict instantaneous harm upon many.

Since the epoch of creation, the world has continually existed as an amalgamation of virtues and vices. Therefore, it is only after thoroughly contemplating and comprehending the true nature of ourselves—who are a composite of good and evil—along with others like us, and the world itself, that one should endeavor to manifest miracles, and indeed, the greatest of miracles. Otherwise, one would be compelled to perpetually perform miracles merely to mitigate the destruction engendered by these very manifestations.

Consequently, the actions performed by both individuals up to that point are rendered futile. It implies that while one created, the other destroyed. Ultimately, neither party is able to achieve anything. This is precisely how those who identify as ascetics act and ultimately face defeat.
Question: Are you referring specifically to mystical powers (*Siddhis*)?

Guru: I am not merely referring to mystical powers, but rather encompassing all aspects of action. None of these ascetics committed these acts with the explicit desire to become wicked. They simply slipped in their actions. If one lacks the innate disposition to act with their mind focused upon the divine presence and aimed at the divine will, this flaw will subtly overtake us without our awareness. It is this specific detriment that afflicts us as we continuously engage in numerous external and internal actions.
Question: In your opinion, what must be done to avert this?

Guru: The directive to avert it is inherently contained within those very words. Did you not notice it? A devotee inherently possesses a distinct qualitative excellence in their disposition. For a yogi, it manifests through the science of yoga. For a person of action (*karmi*), it emerges through their deeds. The seeker of knowledge (*jnani*) possesses it innately. Even though the essence remains the same, the devotee possesses the effortlessness to act with a sense of total surrender; the yogi harbors the mindset that their achievements stem from yogic prowess; whereas the *karmi* holds the attitude of "behold the deed I have accomplished." The *jnani*, however, is capable of recognizing that everyone's actions are correct from their respective standpoints, and can establish that they themselves are the embodiment of that very truth. Experience has proven that only the *jnani* and the devotee can attain this effortlessly.
Question: May we consider this as a self-realized experience?
Guru: You may. However, while considering it as such, one must not deviate from the philosophical discipline by adopting an attitude of "that is their experience, and this is my experience."
Question: What is the reason for saying so?

Guru: Because the devotee, the *jnani*, and the yogi all possess a *sattvic* (pure) nature, they will acknowledge it. Yet, accompanying this is something known as *sattvic* ego. One unknowingly takes pride, assuming that the actions they have performed possess considerable superiority. This tendency has thus emerged and afflicted everyone.

There is evidence that this is ingrained in all of us. There is a tendency in us to say, "It is somewhat acceptable." We also do not say it is completely unacceptable. We use this same expression even for the very best. This flaw primarily occurs in the most intelligent individuals. If it can infiltrate the intellectual, how can we be certain it will not infiltrate us? It will certainly infiltrate us as well. To prevent its entry, the devotee develops an attitude of absolute surrender toward the Guru, recognizing that the previously mentioned path is the sole recourse. The *jnani*, observing the goodness that everything is functioning correctly in its respective place, consistently anchors their sacred actions solely in virtue, and accomplishes them in an ordinary manner without being overwhelmed by the force of that virtue.
Question: I still wish to hear further elucidation on the exact nature of what you are implying through all of this.

Guru: I will have to reiterate what has already been said. Nevertheless, I shall explain it in slightly more detail. In this current *Kali Yuga*, we can only speak by observing its weight and magnitude. Therefore, it can be clarified better only if articulated with that at the forefront. What is your current understanding of the term *Kali*?

Question: It is perceived that *Kali* has deeply entrenched itself within people and everything else. The prevailing belief is that, unable to perform righteous deeds, the innate goodness of humanity will be entirely annihilated.

Guru: That is incorrect. We ourselves assert that we have arrived on this earth in accordance with the results of our past actions (*karma*). If that is the case, does it not imply that the fruits of actions performed incrementally in the *Treta Yuga* and *Dvapara Yuga* will manifest in this *Kali Yuga*?
Question: It will manifest.
Guru: If it is to manifest, shouldn't the virtues cultivated during those eras also manifest?
Question: The virtues must manifest as well.

Guru: If so, isn't acting in the fourth era while evaluating the virtues and vices of the preceding three eras conceived as a state of absorption (*layanathmakam*), where one reaches a state of liberation—devoid of both positive and negative attributes—achieved through the fruits of actions executed with a perfectly balanced understanding of the weight of merits and demerits?
Question: Yes, it is exactly like that. Then, is it your proposition that this era is capable of fully grasping and retaining virtue?

Guru: Yes, certainly. No other three eras offer the opportunity quite like this *Kali Yuga*, where one can strive, perform any action through hardship, and bring it to the forefront. Or even if they do, it is exceedingly delayed. This is precisely why even our ancestral sages desired to be born in the *Kali Yuga* to attain liberation.

Question: Having listened to what you have said thus far, it is to be understood that, by evaluating everything that has transpired until today, an attempt is being made to rectify past anomalies by establishing a system as suited to the times as possible, shaping the forthcoming state of affairs, and bringing it to the forefront, is it not?

Guru: That is precisely the objective. That is also the knowledge we have received. It would require an extensive period to completely implement and consolidate the knowledge we have documented over many days.

In that systemic arrangement, when observing the characteristics of ashrams that have existed until now, our ashram exhibits certain distinctions. Thus far, the practice has been to strictly follow the predecessors and tread the exact path they have shown. All of this needs to be systematized—not partially, but entirely. That is to say, according to Hindu jurisprudence, we have now been entrusted with these three types of worship modalities. To unify the scenario of establishing "one" in the place of all three, one must first comprehend the matter and believe in it. It is only after believing that one will be able to put it into practice.

There are some people for whom outdated methods of worship are ingrained in their flesh, blood, and marrow, clinging tightly to their lives. As soon as faith is first established in this, the concepts of ancestors and the concepts of God they have worshipped thus far should be unified, and with the power they have worshipped, they must be brought into the divine light. Then, in that place, the faith in the Guru must be firmly established again. They must be convinced and believe in what that Guru is. Thus, they must learn to worship with the concept that the Guru is God. Such is the fundamental principle of the Hindu. That is why it begins with 'Gurur Brahma' and concludes with 'Sakshat Para Brahma'. Only if such knowledge is acquired can it be conveyed to the common people.

Therefore, one must know the qualities that this Guru, who is the Supreme Brahman, should possess. He must treat both the wicked and the virtuous equally. He will try to bring the wicked to the right path by afflicting and inflicting pain through their own actions. However, what is shown to the virtuous is also the same. There is only a slight difference. That difference is that even if there are many faults in the actions of the wicked, he will forgive them and let them be. He will not try too hard to correct them. But in the case of the virtuous, he will control them very strictly. If they do not listen when controlled, he will let them go. Why is that? If they deviate even slightly from the path they have ascended, that slight deviation will cause a profound gap within them. If such a gap occurs, it cannot be bridged in that lifetime.

It is keeping that memory in mind that Gurus develop an attitude that even if someone does not become right, it does not matter, let them go. If it is a wicked person, they will think let him fall a bit and then rise up. That is why, in a Guru-disciple relationship understood in this manner, disciples take care not to give room for even a single contradictory word. A Guru lineage that begins to turn in this way will face stages of enduring numerous hardships. Because the course of that lineage seems contrary to what people are accustomed to. For example, if one observes carefully, one can see what kind of revolution occurred when attempts were made to change each existing thing.

If one happens to read at least once the sorrowful truth experienced by the recently emerged Christianity and Buddhism, along with their lineages, it is easy to understand what the people who experienced that pain and their Guru lineages went through. It is because they went through such hardships that their sacrifices have to be valued. Looking at the era we live in today, unless we proceed with a bit more strength and propriety, it will not be possible to bring people to the right path.

Every individual standing involved in the path we intend should assume themselves to be resolute in purpose and that they are the strongest and most appropriate person on this path. Whoever they may be and in whichever path they may live, they must live focusing on that Guru's path. Only if we fully internalize such an ideal can we serve this and create precedents. Otherwise, out of desire or base enmity, one might create a rift and move away.

For that, first truly study this ideal and draw strength from it. Having gained strength, act moderately and come forward through intellectual prowess to advance. It is imperative that every individual possesses all appropriate compromises, outpourings of love, and a wealth of sacrifice. Only such lineages have been able to come forward to date. All those who step into this must be courageous and possess the capable nature to reconcile even those who are estranged through love. If this happens, we can all see a good tomorrow as divinely conceived. This is how our Guru lineage should set its goals.

Especially householders (Grihasthas) should be the ones to become acquainted with this and come forward. Men and women must join together and perform only actions that mutually accommodate each other with love and respect in all endeavors. Thus, the home will attain a place of unity. Through that love, the lineage of offspring will be good, and in imparting the necessary knowledge to the children in that lineage, two or three other conditions will also have to be adopted.

In this regard, one should not consider which caste, which religion, or which class someone belongs to in the Guru lineage. Regardless of how they are, let there be unity. What is achieved through that unity is that they are all like members of one family. Through that, find occupation and create a unified form. Through this, there will be a peace for their life's hardships. The lineage of self-education will become theirs. That culture will be cultivated to a level befitting the lineage. Thus, when their organizational nature becomes one, their sense of unity will also become one. Even if we gather everything for this, there is another nature we must strongly know.

This nature called Guru must be one in whom all the special powers of the divine system have occurred. It is not for us to imitate the path of the gods and goddesses. Without recognizing them and correcting the destruction, one cannot be brought before a Guru. The people must be completely corrected and brought back along the path traditionally taken by our predecessors, the Devas and Rishis themselves. Furthermore, one must have held both the system of Devendra and the position of the lord of the Ganas. They must be ones who have experienced what is called the presence of Ishwara, the presence of God, and the presence of Brahman. Only such a Guru can bring these ideals together.

Question: Hearing what you just said, one must recognize and correct everything from ghosts to Yakshas, Gandharvas, Kinnaras, and the city of Vetalas. What is the way for us to know and correct this here?

Guru: There, it is enough if you accept the word of the Guru exactly as it is. You do not need to correct it. The Guru is one who has borne all of this, right? It is sufficient just not to violate the words of the Guru. Then you can ascend without error.

If one intends to act like the Guru after the Guru's time, one must observe and correct this, learn all of it while the Guru is still present, and stand with wisdom. Otherwise, that movement will stagger for a while after the Guru's time. Then it will cease to exist.
Guruvani
April 1981
Question: So, could that be the reason why most institutions established in this way are seen stagnating after the founder's time?

Guru: Not only because of that. While that person is alive, there are certain things that need to be completely finished. It has to be corrected and completed through experience. Even if known, it becomes difficult to complete them. The reason is that all the human beings living with him are those who have thought and lived contrarily. Then, some differences seen are several poems by those who are called scholars. Thus, experiential matters cannot be imparted through a scholarly nature.

What is called scholarship is like polishing. It is just like building with bricks and painting it white. If those who lived in a well-painted, good building are taken and made to live in a hut, one will see a scene where they cannot even turn around due to disgust and mess. They will not have the knowledge that the mansion originated from a hut like this. It is difficult to see a conscious effort to make the relief of sorrow in between a reality and to maintain the tradition through that karmic power succeed with everything falling into place.

One who brings success in such a manner will have to experience sorrow like Jesus, the Prophet, and Guru Nanak. Contemporaries witnessing all this might see nothing right but only faults in front of them; upon seeing all this, some might decide to remain silent. Some will work a little and stop. Seeing such things, quite a few will withdraw, saying, 'Didn't you see so-and-so acting and getting ruined?' When hearing what those without this inclination say, assuming it to be right, everything gets pushed into despair.
Question: You mentioned some states from the city of Vetalas to the world of Devas. There is a desire to know how that can be explained as well.
*Continued from the previous issue

Guru: It is difficult to comprehend that precisely. This is because only the masters who are born in accordance with the times will attain this completely. Others might attain it to a certain extent, but they will never grasp its complete dimensions. The knowledge required to observe and act from the very origin of the universe cannot be simply transformed into exceptional intellect. Even if one observes it, they will not obtain all the favorable circumstances required to execute and fulfill it. What else can be done then? One can only stop right there, isn't it?

Once the realm of Vethala (Vethalanagaram) is crossed, a somewhat worthy state is achieved in the subsequent stages. That is, the departure towards the state of deities. That state will be seen as completely radiant. What one immediately receives is an easy path within the Trimurti system. The reason for attaining this is the positive things received as a rest from what happened prior to it. Before successfully crossing the realm of Vethala, we will have to experience and realize numerous sorrowful truths. The stones and thorns placed by God for this purpose are our contemporary human beings and even other creatures in this earthly world.

The only difference between them and him lies in good thoughts and good deeds. Everything else is exactly the same. He will experience all the powers of that demon through his contemporary humans. They will view him as Hiranyakashipu. Words cannot express the difficulty in rectifying this widespread distress, which is as incompatible as milk and horse gram. However, attaining a position in this state of ascending to the deities serves as an interval of relief. To all other believers, he will be perceived just like the Trimurtis. Having seen this much, one cannot be faulted for unknowingly becoming arrogant, feeling, "I have become everything." However, neither this experienced individual nor the society that accepted him in a mimicking manner upon seeing his qualifications will be able to realize that all this merely demonstrates the cyclical and repetitive nature of the heavenly world.

What happens here is neither anyone's fault nor merit. It is a place where such things naturally occur. If one looks at what the Puranas say about Kailasa, one can see what kind of luxurious traits and antics are described! You will understand that when you read the Shiva Purana. There are other Puranas that speak about the Vaishnavas. If you read about that, it is even grander. Thus, if you examine each Purana, you will find that the essential matters occupy only a very small portion of them. Transcending all this and bringing it to a resolution—as proclaimed by the Puranas themselves—takes multiple lifetimes. In our experience, this is also largely true. Overcoming all these means that a soul, which has been led purely and holily through lifetimes, will eventually reside in certain divine realms. Sometimes we hear the names of stars, don't we? Like the Shukra star, Velli star (Venus), and Arundhati star. There are many such stars, both large and small. There are those that are much larger than the Earth and those that are much smaller. It may not be possible to meticulously comprehend and analyze all of these.
Question: What should we understand from your words about what needs to be done here next?

Guru: Haven't you understood from what has been said so far? Isn't it clear that these celestial spheres stand beyond nine realms, similar to Earth? Beyond knowing about these star systems and all this, there is a higher state. Only then can this be known. Even at the very first stage of this Trimurti system, one is seeing and experiencing almost up to the state of Godhead. Do you think it is possible to experience, realize, and describe this, or to accomplish and conclude any one of these tasks?
Question: From what I have heard, I can understand that it is indeed difficult.

Guru: When it is this difficult to repeatedly accomplish even good things, imagine the magnitude of difficulty in knowing and realizing the qualities contradictory to everything we mentioned earlier. When he begins to repeatedly realize this, all his contemporary people who respected him and considered him good—even those who sang his praises until then—will look at him with disdain. They will act with enmity, torment him in every possible way, and drag him down, piling misery upon him. Eventually, only a cluster of these heaps will be seen. If one carefully examines history, one can see numerous great men who, despite working for the good, were transformed into something worse than beasts. One need not even look at history. Can't we see it if we look at the contemporary nature of today?
Question: Yes, we can see that.
Guru: Do you know how all of that is seen through us?
Question: I have understood it. But it is not clear how exactly it happens.

Guru: Currently, aren't you seeing a lot in the papers regarding various believers, rationalists, different godmen (Bawas), and the evaluations of scholars? Haven't you understood what all this implies? It means that no one can truly recognize anyone else. Just like in the past, each person is slipping from one state of blindness into another even now.
Question: Then, in your opinion, how should this be corrected?

Guru: Here, what is needed now is not correction, but realization. Will anyone among those mentioned admit that they are flawed? If anyone in the world says that one particular group among them is bad or anything of the sort, they will all gang up and resort to untoward actions. Each of the godmen is clever. The college professors and principals here are all qualified for their respective positions. The religious scholars and authors of the Puranas here are also qualified. Then there is a specific section of people who believe that only the Vedas and Upanishads are right. What they say is above all this. And then there are the rationalists and salvation-seekers, who act as if they have mixed all this up and swallowed it whole. Does someone who knows a little bit and tries to speak have any standing? There is a venomous breed of wasps. It would be fortunate if all of these people don't act like them, spreading toxicity and finishing him off right here.

However, one cannot say that all this is wrong. It must be called right. If one discerns all this at a glance, the subjects appear in a way that suggests the right is slightly more prevalent. When examining the Puranas and stories, these godmen, such gurus, rationalists, and salvation-seekers are souls who have been repeatedly born and died over countless ages. If we observe closely, we can see whether they are the ones who have returned repeatedly in this era. Behind this is another group that pretends everything happens through them. All this is the growth of science. Can we, who experience and understand it to a large extent, say it is wrong? Similarly, if time moves forward a little, they will have to admit that a lot of this is flawed.

For example, by the time the medicines discovered, tested, and released through laboratories are used on the public, they begin to declare them as flawed. Thus, they have reached a stage where they do not hesitate to declare things as right or wrong every second. Another group is standing firm here, ready to repeatedly assert that all this is correct. Recently, with the fall of Skylab, a lot of panic spread across the world, and numerous opinions regarding this have surfaced among the people.

Shouldn't we understand that all this is causing some kind of disruption and that a danger lurks behind it? We are already experiencing the reality that numerous toxic gases have spread in the atmosphere, affecting humans and all living beings, causing various diseases. One must suspect whether purity of character itself has become akin to some sort of machine. It is bound to happen that way. Because, there is no doubt that consuming plants and food materials grown under the influence of these gases will affect not only our bodies but our intellect as well.

We have overt empirical evidence laid out before us to substantiate this. The artists in our midst are virtually incapable of writing or performing unless they consume a specific kind of intoxicant. Once a small quantity of it is ingested, melodies flow spontaneously. Dance movements may ensue, whether they align with classical aesthetics or not. They attempt to compensate for bodily grace at least through exaggerated contortions. As this tendency proliferated, it eventually permeated even the ranks of healthcare professionals; consequently, if patients were to awaken suddenly from an unconscious state and behold these individuals—whose appearances make it indiscernible whether they should be regarded as doctors or the deity of death—they might instantly succumb to sheer terror. Perhaps this explains why certain patients die immediately upon regaining consciousness post-surgery. This remains our only logical conjecture. Those lying sedated under the influence of narcotics are essentially lying frozen in the proximity of death.

Deep within the patient's psyche, the preconceived mythological narratives concerning the God of Death would instantly rush to the forefront. Consequently, their breath would cease. A minority devoid of such preconceptions might somehow survive. By the same token, the ominous formations emanating from these toxic gases might congregate in certain regions of this atmosphere. Once congregated, they possess the potential to precipitate any magnitude of catastrophe from the skies. It is entirely superfluous to state what might transpire thereafter!

Question: You articulated earlier that certain individuals are forcefully stepping forward to assert that everything is absolutely correct. I have not entirely comprehended the meaning of that statement.

Guru: In our society, a fervent race for education is perpetually disseminating among both the impoverished and the affluent classes. Generally, the progeny of the highly affluent do not engage in rigorous academic pursuits. They acquire degrees by leveraging financial power or through other means; ultimately, their primary destination is the political arena. They envision themselves as leaders. Automobiles and airplanes are placed at their absolute disposal without them even demanding it. Observing such privileges induces a state of euphoria that leaves individuals completely ungrounded. For whom does this happen? The descendants of the profoundly impoverished—those who lack adequate sustenance and clothing—also grasp the edge of politics under the influence of this euphoric illusion. They aspire to become leaders. The superficial rhetoric they have heard and witnessed metamorphoses into their ideological principles. Observing these dynamics, a select few individuals recognize this as an opportune mechanism and swiftly infiltrate the political sphere. Upon their arrival, they manipulate the masses by validating their actions as absolutely correct, eventually ascending to become the leaders of the existing leadership. Consequently, by asserting claims ranging from the trivial to the monumental, they reduce the populace to mere peripheral sentinels and commence their governance. This specific faction epitomizes the ultimate embodiment of those who actively rationalize these systemic anomalies as fundamentally correct. Viewed from this perspective, does it not become evident that our pervasive toxic influences have extinguished the vital consciousness within all living entities? Contemplating this paradigm, one is left with no alternative but to assert that all of this is absolutely correct.
Question: If all of this is deemed absolutely correct, what then is the implication for how we are supposed to navigate this?
Guru: The question is indeed valid. I am inclined to believe that your comprehension of this matter is akin to asserting that a tortoise possesses the fur of a camel.

Question: It is nothing of that sort. I posed the question merely to attain clarity. I have exhausted myself reading the Puranas and the Upanishads. I have yet to ascertain where the foundational crux of this actually lies.

Guru: I have repeatedly elucidated this to you in the past. One of the profoundly informative forms, born periodically in accordance with the Yugas, transformed into enlightened sages through their supreme sacrifice and divine grace. Posthumously, for the life forces radiating from various sacred planets and stellar constellations, only those sons who are born by divine providence—guided by the disembodied celestial voice that reminds them of the luminous verses of the Gita, the Upanishads, and the Vedic proclamations—can accomplish this through divine grace alone. These profound truths cannot be acquired merely through instruction, regardless of whether one is categorized as a scholar, a layman, or an intellectual. These revelations remain entirely inaccessible to both the rationalist and the mere seeker of salvation. Therefore, let us conclude these particular segments here. Expounding further will only transcend your comprehension.
Guruvani
May 1981
Question: You had previously indicated that Krishna is the incarnate deity of a specific Yuga!

Guru: That is correct. The era of Krishna signifies the commencement of one Yuga and the culmination of another. However, prior to deliberating upon Krishna, certain other matters necessitate clarification. Numerous great souls were born prior to Krishna and conducted themselves in accordance with the prevailing Yuga. Yet, even before that, certain systemic anomalies persisted. A Shudra sage was assassinated with an arrow. Concurrently, the rigid caste system, internal sub-castes, and a monarchical regime that systematically deprived specific populations even of basic literacy were forcefully instituted.

Under the dominion of a single monarch, one specific group of subjects was permitted to acquire literacy, whereas another group was strictly prohibited from doing so. How did such a paradigm come into existence? Consequently, it is unequivocally clear that these structural anomalies existed long before. The reality of diverse categories of subjects existing under a single monarch is the direct consequence of strategic political maneuvers, whereby a certain demographic was systematically ostracized and expelled to seize control of the governing apparatus. Those who complied were granted everything, while the dissenters were brutally subjugated and driven away. If observed meticulously, one can discern the remnants of such exclusionary tactics in contemporary administrative structures even today.

It is observable that the scholars who authored the history of Kerala during the period of India's independence conspicuously omitted prominent leaders. If such historiographical distortions occur in the present era, one can only hypothesize the magnitude of manipulations orchestrated by the governing bodies of antiquity. During that epoch, an absolute decree was established forbidding a Shudra from listening to the Vedas. It was precisely for this reason that the Shudra sage was systematically denied the fundamental right to pursue asceticism. If subjects residing under a sovereign's rule are utterly deprived of their right to perform penance and worship the divine, one cannot even fathom the depths of degradation they would invariably descend into. This is the calculated handiwork perpetrated by the adherents of such exclusionary religious paradigms. We must critically analyze the multitude of malicious intentions they deliberately executed. We are already cognizant of historical narratives that are not too distant in the past. Have we not recently witnessed the actions of the Pakistani administration as well?
*Continued from the previous issue

What all transpirations occurred when Marthanda Varma assumed control of our Travancore monarchy? Men were systematically annihilated, and women were captured and forcibly handed over to the fisherfolk. Consequently, as they fled to various kingdoms in desperation, it is documented that they sought refuge in regions such as Karunagappally, Karthikappally, and Vaikom. Their inherent aristocratic dignity and aesthetic grace remain undiminished even today. The lineage of Chempil Arayan, renowned for the traditional snake boats, continues to live with immense respectability. One can also observe Brahmins and others partaking in meals while seated in distinctly separate rows. When such overwhelming evidence remains tangibly present, there is absolutely no doubt that history has been fundamentally distorted. In such oppressive circumstances, as a direct consequence of internalizing a corrupted culture devoid of any authoritative access to the Vedas, none of the individuals from the Shudra caste downwards have been able to achieve genuine emancipation or rectitude.

Since the other two Yugas (Treta Yuga and Dwapara Yuga) constituted the epoch of the Devas, it was entirely feasible to conceptualize the deity and perform divine worship. The fourth Yuga constitutes the ultimate seat of authority for all of this. If the other three Yugas have sequentially progressed in strict accordance with their specific Yuga Dharma, and if one possesses faith in that cosmic order, is it not an absolute certainty that the fourth Yuga must execute its own inherent Dharma? If the Puranas emphatically celebrate that gods and goddesses hold no designated position within the Dharma of the fourth Yuga, is it not an absolute imperative that this cosmic mandate be actualized? Stating that Shudras shall wield governance during the Kali Yuga is not merely a concept to be comprehended; one must inevitably concede when it is asserted that the profound authority over the Vedas also fundamentally belongs to them. Furthermore, by meticulously hoarding these privileges and subjecting us to the indignities of polyandrous alliances devoid of recognized paternity, we have been systematically reduced to our current deplorable state. Delving further into this matter will necessitate extensive discourse. Is it not unequivocally evident that by monopolizing such authoritative domains, the marginalized subjects at the absolute bottom of the hierarchy were systematically disenfranchised and displaced?

There has been a change since the time of Krishna. As mentioned earlier, Krishna's period is at the end of one yuga and the beginning of another. That is, at the end of Dvapara and the beginning of Kali Yuga. We celebrate Onam here, don't we? It is grandly celebrated in Kerala. When a good royal administration existed here, they concocted stories of God appearing and coming here, along with tales of sages, passing them around to create a logical justification. We are taught fabricated stories that someone was pushed into the netherworld just by the touch of a foot. We have also enjoyed listening to them. Certainly, that noble king who ruled well was loved by the people. Therefore, doesn't this prove that the intelligent Brahmin fabricated a story to show that even God is hostile to someone who does good, killed him, seized that royal court, and then made the one who wrote stories for the king at that time create this mockery?

Looking at it this way, one can see such an appearance of God in the house of the King of Pandalam as well. God appears and does what is necessary only when calamities befall the women in the king's house. Looking at the history they have written, it seems that God does not appear to any poor people in our homes. Mahabali, who belonged to the Asura race, was stomped upon; as soon as he was touched, he went to the netherworld. That is how God comes to touch. Thus, as soon as a woman in the king's house got a headache, Mahavishnu and Shiva set out together. When they arrived here, since the woman was unwell, both of them engaged in absurdity, and immediately [the offspring] fell out by splitting the thigh. It was not even a direct birth. Immediately, he mounted a leopard and went into the forest. He caught and tied up a leopard, brought it back, milked it endlessly, and cured the disease. There was a time here when royal administration and the worship of God were conducted through such absurdities. Since the people were illiterate, it was not difficult to weave these stories and make them believe them.

There is evidence for this. There is a history of Ayyappan coming and staying in an Ezhava family in the Cheerappanchira house in Cherthala and teaching Kalaripayattu there. During that time, he also gave advice to a girl there. After that, he went from there to a place called Kanjiramattom Mosque. There he taught Kalaripayattu to Muslims and gave advice to a Muslim youth. At the same time, he went and stayed at the place where the Arthunkal Church is situated today, and facilitated various benefits for many people there. It can be seen that Christians still preserve its memory today. Anyone can be convinced of these facts by going to these places and investigating.

After that, he went to Kanjirappally via Kottayam. It was a place where a group of Brahmins lived at that time. All these Brahmins together took Ayyappan to the King of Pandalam. Upon going there, seeing that he was brilliant and an ascetic, he was made to stay there and entrusted with the responsibility of teaching Kalaripayattu. On that occasion, Ayyappan heard the stories of Vavar, Kochukadutha, and Valiyakkadutha. Thus, one day when Ayyappan went to see the hill, he met Vavar, Kochukadutha, and Valiyakkadutha and gave them advice.

Prior to that, there was a temple there consecrated by a Brahmachari from the royal family. A trench was dug to stay upon arriving there, and a temple was built in the middle of it. To see this, he took them along and went to the place of the Sastha idol, which was a conceptual consecration. The Brahmachari from the royal family - named Hariharan - consecrated it with the conception that his family should become like the Buddha's family in the future, and attained Samadhi right there. An idol of Ganapathi was consecrated over the Samadhi. It was during this time that this Ayyappan arrived and performed penance.

Ayyappan gained power by performing penance over this consecration and Samadhi. Then Kochukadutha, Valiyakkadutha, and Vavar all came down to the king. They had taken control of all the properties there. When the king inquired how to get this back, Ayyappan agreed to sort it out by talking to them. Because Ayyappan was convinced that they would listen if he spoke, as they were his disciples. Thus, the king's men, Vavar, and Ayyappan came to an agreement, and they surrendered the forest wealth. They were also given some land.

In this, Vavar emerged prominent. In the settlement, a condition was placed that one should go to see Ayyappan's Samadhi place only after seeing Vavar's Samadhi place. That is how the 'Saranam' chanting originated, which perpetuates the memory of Kochukadutha, Valiyakkadutha, and Vavar.

Through penance, Ayyappan became greater than this Hariharan and the conceptual consecration. Thus, it could be seen that Sabari stood as a support and shade for this Ayyappan. There is a custom where all first-time Ayyappan devotees take an arrow from Vavar's Samadhi place and place it at the spot of the Saramkuthi banyan tree. That banyan tree is not there today. The one that stood very large was destroyed. Since it is the place where Sabari performed penance, ghee and coconut are offered there. It can still be seen like a homa kunda today. Ayyappan attained Samadhi at the temple precincts. The girl from Cheerappanchira, to whom Ayyappan had given advice during his lifetime, went and met another disciple, the Thangal of Kanjiramattom, and the two of them met Vavar, and everyone together went to Ayyappan. They left that girl there and returned. The temple known today as Malikappuram is where this girl stayed and was interred in Samadhi.

The aforementioned Thangal is the one who attained Samadhi at Kanjiramattom. Today, the family members of this Thangal are traditionally known as the Thangals of Kanjiramattom. Muslims are well aware that the Thangal who attained Samadhi at the Kanjiramattom Mosque is a disciple of Ayyappan. At the Kanjiramattom Mosque, the flag hoisting is on the first of Makaram. At the same time, the doors of Ayyappan's shrine are closed after the lamp lighting on that day. After a very long case in the name of the girl from Cheerappanchira, the High Court granted the right to fire ceremonial shots. The upper-caste hegemony seized that as well again. Stating that such a right should not belong to a household like this and that it is inferior, they filed a case in the court. The right to fire shots was canceled. This was done by the Devaswom Board. This is a recent example of upper-caste hegemony.

Who is this Ayyappan? A boy belonging to a carpenter family in the Palakkad district in North Malabar. His father and mother died when he was three years old. Many households adopted and raised him. Eventually, he learned Kalaripayattu and other things, the martial arts deities appeared, and through that, he almost attained Siddhi. All these things happened while he set out on an ascetic path. This is the history of Ayyappan. (Have you heard the Saranam chanting in the name of this Ayyappan? They will not lie. But they will show a trick - they call out 'Harihara Sutan Ayyanayyappaswami'. It means that Ayyappan, who was Ayyan, became Ayyappaswami. Hariharan is the Brahmachari from the royal family, the Sastha, the conceptual consecration that was there.) If this can be distorted and done like this, isn't it the truth that the poets of that time distorted history and handled it in this way? Isn't it proven that such histories were distorted carefully so that their hegemony would not be lost? Most of the poets of that time belonged to Brahmin families and were authorities in the royal family. The other illiterate people - growing like wild grass - do they know this? From so much evidence existing like this, isn't it understood what all destructions this Varnasrama Dharma has caused?
Question: Where did you get this much history from?

Guru: This history is not just this. There is a lot. That cannot be said. It was just indicated for the knowledge of the people. I have said, haven't I - that many things have been told through philosophical visions, which cannot be revealed now. I have also said that after my time, if there are people who believe in this, let them reveal it.
Guruvani
June 1981
Question: You started talking about Sree Krishna earlier and stopped, didn't you? I am interested to know what that is.

Guru: According to the laws of Manu, five gurus emerge during a single epoch (*Yuga*). When two epochs are combined, eleven gurus appear. Sri Krishna is the eleventh guru in the combined span of the *Treta Yuga* and *Dvapara Yuga*.
Question: Is it not the case that Sri Krishna is traditionally referred to as a deity (*Deva*)?

Guru: Generally, conferring the status of a deity was the prevailing practice. Elevating him to the status of a deity was a necessity for the survival of the Brahmins. They perpetually maintained a specific form of worship exclusively for themselves. They remain the sole officiants of rituals in any temple. Furthermore, they reserve certain specialized rituals strictly for their own households. Consider the great Lord Venkateshwara—the idol lacks a distinct nose and eyes. The adorning of sacred ornaments and the complete coating with sandalwood paste (*muzhukkappu*) are conducted in a highly specialized manner. A figure is drawn by concealing the facial features such as the eyes.

Appropriating anything of value as their own was an integral part of their strategy. They have consistently preserved this approach throughout history. Even today, regardless of the political party or organization one examines, they can be found positioning themselves as the authoritative figures over any non-caste-based entity. They operate as the dominant elites in society, securing a position that sustains their influence. Following the lifetimes of the gurus from the *Parayi Petta Panthirukulam*, they authored verses retrospectively assimilating these figures into the Brahmin fold. Historical records indicate that during the lifetimes of these gurus, there was a profound reluctance to either associate with them or to accord any canonical status to their poetic works.
* Continued from the previous issue

Historical accounts suggest that even prior to Sri Krishna's birth, anticipating the emergence of such a profound force, efforts were made to thwart it. Eventually, they themselves developed the conviction that Sri Krishna was perfected by his very birth. It was also established that he was a profoundly wise being. When his preeminence became evident through his birth and maturation, they began to disseminate writings that, while perhaps not overtly abusive in tone, subtly undermined him through the citation of specific narratives. The advent of Sri Krishna provided the world with a magnificent figure who upheld the highest standards of morality and sanctity within the prevailing socio-cultural system of that era. He accomplished this by assimilating all the pre-existing virtues, honoring and cementing them, thereby fulfilling the ultimate purpose of his incarnation. A singular incident narrated in the epic account of the eighteen-day war serves as conclusive evidence for this. Since he aligned himself with truth, it is evident that he possessed absolute clarity regarding the purpose of his mission. He relinquished his entire army and armaments to the Kauravas, choosing to stand entirely alone alongside Arjuna. Assuming the role of Arjuna's aide, he guided him through profound discourse and impelled him to wage the war. Had he been a mere deity, he would have directly engaged in the conflict himself. To a guru, all individuals are fundamentally equal; however, desiring the ultimate victory of truth, a guru invariably aligns with it.

Following the advent of Krishna, they invoke names such as Krishna, Kalki, and Janardhana. These concepts have largely transformed into subsequent interpolations within the Hindu tradition. There have been concerted efforts to deify figures like Sri Ramakrishna, Sri Narayana Guru, and various eminent personalities from North India as divine incarnations (*Avataras*). A similar narrative is propagated by some concerning Chattampi Swami. Nevertheless, one might plausibly contend that the manifestation of the Kalki *Avatara* has already occurred. Elements such as the sword and shield are notably prominent within the lineage of Guru Nanak. Aside from the traditions of Christianity and Islam, they represent a distinct lineage adhering strictly to the structural discipline of a guru tradition or prophethood. Mainstream orthodoxy refuses to acknowledge this, dismissing it on the grounds that it effectively established a separate religion. Regardless of these contentions, it remains an undeniable historical reality that this phenomenon occurred within India itself.

Many religions, such as Jainism and Buddhism, have originated in India. Among them, they are reluctant even to admit that this occurred in India. The reason for this is that it possesses a character distinct from Hinduism. Even upon joining the military, they have been granted the right to retain their traditional headgear and swords. Although they depicted Krishna as a deity and added many other elements while writing his story, they circulated a mere fabricated myth among the common people—the myth of him being the husband of sixteen thousand and eight women.

If such a narrative is presented to the common masses, how would these innocent people perceive this individual? Those with limited knowledge will merely remain entangled within this orchestrated scheme, unsure of what to do. For them to acquire knowledge, all aspects of wisdom have been compiled and restricted to the recitation of the *Gita*. Others are strictly forbidden from even viewing it. They have guarded the Vedas in a similar manner, and the same applies to the Upanishads.
Question: There is no prohibition against reading the *Gita*, is there?

Guru: There is no explicit prohibition against reading it. However, you are aware that those in the lower strata of society were historically denied even the right to basic literacy. In a context where even basic literacy was denied to a *Shudra*, perhaps only one in a hundred thousand people from other communities would have possessed knowledge of epics like the *Mahabharata* and the *Ramayana*, or profound texts like the *Gita*.

Today, the general assumption is that everyone is familiar with the *Gita*. But how many people actually read the *Gita*? A few individuals might attend and listen to discourses on the *Gita* where they are held, and that is the extent of it. One should reflect on how extensively the Sanskrit *Gita* has been mastered in languages like Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, or Tulu. It has gained some traction in Hindi, primarily due to the lack of significant differences in the script.

If one observes closely, they will realize whether such widespread propagation of the *Gita* existed prior to the last sixty years. However, until recently, there was widespread familiarity with texts like the *Narayaneeyam*. That is no longer the case; the *Gita* has now been brought to the forefront. What was the underlying motive behind circulating a degrading fabrication among the poor regarding a great personality who possessed the rights to such a monumental text? It should not be naively dismissed as an act done out of ignorance. This remains one of the most monumental farces perpetrated through the cunning manipulation of knowledge.

Certain historical accounts state that Krishna married eight women. That might also have been due to the societal conditions of that era, which dictated that unmarried girls should not interact too closely with men. Similarly, the history of the Prophet mentions that he married ten women. This is why they are referred to as the luminaries of their respective epochs. Whatever is required for that epoch, be it good or bad, they must demonstrate it before their departure. It is for this precise reason that such marriages were demonstrated. Krishna was one who attained eight such states. Similarly, it is stated that the Prophet had to marry to fulfill this specific state. This is an act compelled by nature itself—perhaps implying that they had a specific cosmic mandate to fulfill. Merely because such a perspective exists in Islam, a local *beedi* roller or a fishmonger attempts to equate himself with the Prophet and marries ten times. Similarly, citing the example of Panchali, people in southern Travancore can be seen marrying up to five times. They fail to emulate or even glance at any of the other profound actions demonstrated by these great figures.

This group of people has not displayed even the slightest inclination to contemplate why these great figures acted in such ways. Whether dealing with a king or a divine incarnation, unless the label of 'Brahminism' is attached to them, some form of deceit will inevitably be concealed within their historical narratives. The narrative surrounding Maveli serves as a prime example of this. By examining the extensive efforts made to confer *Kshatriya* status upon rulers from other castes at this end of the country, one can comprehend the extent of the manipulations they have orchestrated. To prevent the loss of their divine status, they intellectually engineered structures like the *Amarakosha*, beginning with 'Amara Nirjara Deva', completely consolidating their narrative. They even managed to subtly integrate texts like the *Siddharoopam*, which cost a mere eight *kashu* in Travancore at the time, into this grand scheme. Consequently, irrespective of the context, anyone operating within this linguistic framework is inextricably bound to the concept of the deity.

In order to prevent the loss of such Vedic authority, the *Varnashrama Dharma* has been preserved to this day. The *Gita* itself states that in the *Kali Yuga*, there will be an intermingling of castes (*Sankara*). Why, then, should one adhere to the *Varnashrama Dharma* today? Today, poetry is hybridized. When even a plant growing in the courtyard is experienced as a hybrid, what exactly are we trying to achieve with this *Varnashrama Dharma*? If one examines this meticulously, the trajectory up to the present day demonstrates that throughout the extensive duration of this *Kali Yuga*, the lifespans of all human beings will be guided toward an ultimate reality where only liberation (*Mukti*) and the divine (*Deva*) hold authority.
Question: What did you mean by stating "only liberation and the divine"?

Guru: That is to say, it has been elucidated thus far that those who follow the absolute Guru lineage attain liberation, whereas those who follow alternative paths are granted multiple incarnations, elevating them at least to the stature of a deity. As an illustration of this, even if the realization that human rights are universal for all individuals has not been entirely achieved, the conviction has been firmly established.

It has become government legislation that education is accessible to all human beings. The government has facilitated this by providing financial assistance. Consequently, there is no doubt that over time, all forms of knowledge will become universally accessible. Once knowledge, wealth, and intellectual awakening have been comprehensively attained, humanity will reflect, "Despite possessing all these, a state of tranquil peace has not been achieved; let us investigate this." Once knowledge, wealth, and intellect are equitably attained, human endeavor will be directed toward peace. There is absolute certainty that they will attain and perfect it unconsciously. Should these aspirations remain unfulfilled over ten or twelve generations, the world may descend into profound chaos in ten to two hundred years. If such a state of stagnation occurs, nature might manifest an opportunity, akin to the immediate influx of water following the introduction of salt, resulting in the birth of exalted souls capable of inherently transforming the situation. Hoping that, instead of compelling such an intervention through divine glory, all sections of our society may be inspired to utilize our endowed intellect and capabilities to earnestly comprehend and act in accordance with the divine will, I shall conclude for the present.
Guruvani
July 1981
Question: From what you have just concluded, it would appear to those with some intellect that this is being stated with immense resentment.

Guru: There is resentment, unequivocally. Would I appreciate my contemporaries deteriorating in any manner? If I possessed a home and a family, would I remain a passive observer if they committed an error? I would endeavor to rectify it to the best of my abilities. If there were a mother, a sister, or close relatives, and it was understood that their actions were detrimental to them, to me, and to the populace, I would alter it. Currently, none of that exists. Presently, devotion to God is not juxtaposed with malevolence. It aligns with benevolence and the elements that sustain it. Consequently, one naturally gravitates toward realms where goodness prevails.

Simultaneously, is it feasible to comprehensively reprimand those who exhibit malevolence? A peculiar perversion that diverts everyone toward malevolence is permeating us. It is observable in everyone, irrespective of distinctions such as scholar or ignoramus, ascetic or yogi, sage, devotee, or man of action.

Just because it is the truth, is it possible to approach everyone and state it directly? Even if articulated, there would scarcely be anyone to heed it. Observing certain things induces agony. Observing others evokes sympathy. There are numerous instances where one is distressed by the sheer obstinacy of certain individuals. In the context of enduring such agony over an extended period by witnessing myriad such occurrences, all these individuals possess distinct capabilities within this world. None of them were deficient in exercising their intellect. If, by divine grace, their intellect could be redirected even marginally toward a virtuous path, is it possible to articulate the immense asset it would be, not solely for us, but for the entire world? Is not the existence of such souls in this world a profound truth that perpetually disseminates eternal peace?

Individuals who harbor the notion that it is sufficient for themselves or for you need not entertain such thoughts. There are countless multitudes in the world. Would it not suffice for ten or twenty-five of them? The nature of devotion to God, or God's love, cannot be comprehensively delineated in any measure. Consequently, the capabilities born of such love manifest in myriad forms. Love resides in everyone. Elevating that love to the pinnacle of its realization can only be accomplished through unceasing vigilance. I do not believe there exists anything comparable to that divine love. It might be owing to the fact that I have become such a believer that these sentiments have emerged. Otherwise, it is my conviction that my words would never exhibit a vindictive nature toward anyone. Perceiving everything through the love that constitutes true knowledge, resolving the deficiencies of existence through actions rooted in that knowledge, acquiring merit in its stead, and ultimately transcending both merit and demerit—if there is an 'I', I perceive it merely as one among billions of offspring, one among billions of living entities. All of this is encompassed within Your glory; You are the truth and the untruth of the world; You Yourself are Sat, Chit, and Ananda—I have merely articulated words aspiring to merge into that state. My sole aspiration is that God may bless all His children to attain this.

Question: The world today appears to be in a precipitous rush with such a revolutionary disposition. What might be the underlying cause? Wherever one observes, religiously and politically, there is a conspicuous absence of tranquility, and actions seem to have devolved into a state of profound uncertainty.

Guru: We should lament only if the populace had not evolved into this state. Observing the progression and regression of the world, this is absolutely imperative for the present epoch. If we remain complacent, assuming that what has been discovered thus far holds some validity, it will prove more detrimental than the preceding conditions. If we concede that what existed previously was valid to an extent, it would culminate in a trajectory that plunges the entire world into obscurity. This is because, oppressed by the tyranny of monarchies, feudal hegemonies, and tenant servitude, caste and religion intensified to their utmost extremes, rendering life entirely bestial. Thus, an ideological quest for liberty fostered a political tension here. None of these aforementioned political enthusiasts emerged by discovering a traditional foundation and seeking to sustain it. Their selflessness, born of witnessing the myriad afflictions and losses of the people, engendered a desire to enact some form of liberation. That is the zenith of their capabilities. Within that paradigm of thought, they progressed—stumbling and recovering—achieving some commendable outcomes while inadvertently precipitating subsequent chaos.

This is an absolute distortion unconsciously assimilated within them, fueled by their egoistic assertions of supremacy, comprising a faction that rejects everything unequivocally and another that accepts everything indiscriminately. When disparate types of leaders were embraced within this matrix, numerous followers blindly enlisted and began unconsciously spouting ideologies. They are ostensibly valorous individuals who remain utterly ignorant of the essence of sacrifice or its fundamental nature.

There is a contingent of individuals who endorse them—destitute people lacking both education and wealth. They implicitly believe whatever is articulated by those they harbor affection for. By aggregating all such vulnerable individuals, a numerical dominance is manufactured. Observing this, the leaders who initially instigated the movement reigned as idealists and leaders for a significant duration. Embellishments and altercations continue to proliferate, creating the illusion that this constitutes the absolute reality of the world. This is the unbridled manifestation of the resentment against the tyranny of the feudal lords and tenants we alluded to earlier. Such distortions will inevitably permeate this process. It is inconsequential. In that frenetic race, even if contemporaries advocate for righteousness, it may not be implemented. Because in an unrestrained surge, this too shall dissipate. Such a pursuit is merely akin to arriving at the seashore and reveling in the sight of the horizon. A state of stagnation will inevitably ensue. A predicament will befall them wherein they can neither retreat nor maneuver from their current position.

Such a juncture will precipitate a phase that rectifies the world's antecedent deficiencies. Thus, as a consequence of this multifaceted and suffocating chaotic trajectory, analogous to the populace heaving a sigh of relief, the temporal manifestation of divine will shall promptly arrive at that precise moment. Then, these aberrations will autonomously recede or be eradicated from religious leaders and mass leaders. Much like the dissolution of numerous monarchies and feudal regimes, it will transpire imperceptibly. Concurrently, an embodiment of the divine will shall emerge. Subsequently, a period characterized by conflicts and disputes over its respective ideologies will persist. For a duration, an intense fervor to implement it will be exhibited. Akin to insatiable desires, it will necessitate a considerable epoch to achieve consummation. When it is thus realized over an extended period, the intrinsic worth of this era will be unequivocally affirmed.
Question: Does this period refer to the Kali Yuga?
Guru: Yes, it refers to the Kali Yuga.
Question: Then, what is meant by this Kali?
Guru: We mean that there will be absolute goodness at the end of Kali.
Question: Certainly, goodness. What is the reason for calling it absolute goodness?

Guru: That has already been stated. As you know, Kali Yuga is the end of the Chatur Yuga. The early period of Kali is an evaluation of the good and evil of the other three past eras. Moreover, it could be that this evaluation is reached over ten or twenty-five thousand years.
Question: Does this evaluation refer to previous births?
Guru: Absolutely, it does.
Question: Then we can firmly believe that there are numerous births, right?
Guru: Yes, you can believe exactly that.
Question: How can this be made believable to the people?
Guru: The people can be completely convinced of this. It is just that today, very few people are interested in thinking about and understanding such subjects.
Question: Then how is this fully implemented?

Guru: Did we not say earlier that there are instances in history where, after running aimlessly for a long time and hitting a dead end, a certain nature gained some acceptance? Similar to that, this will also have its turn. It will be considered like a firm resolve that has grown and risen through fluctuations. Thus, I am telling you in the light of experience that this will be brought to a good path. It will also attain a complete form, just like what exists politically and religiously now. Consequently, in humans who discover this, honesty, humility, and the competence to practice them will reach their full potential. It will be utilized for the peace and survival of humanity. However, that will last for a long time. The era known as Satya Yuga will be shifted to the next Chatur Yuga.
Question: The essence of what you are saying is that it will grow in this manner and complete the era of each Manu, isn't it?
Guru: Yes.

Question: But a certain group of people will not even take a peek at the independent nature you mentioned, right? It is true that you said ordinary people will run after it. However, a specific group does not usually even look at it.
Guru: It would be good if you explained a little more. I do not understand who you mean by "a certain group of people."

Question: Although everyone here talks about progress today, it is shown that there is no progress even in their names. A sweeping term like 'Harijans'. Another approach like 'backward Christians'. We only see one community here that cannot be described in any other way. A class called Islam. If the downtrodden person who is called Thevar or Kali today becomes an Islamic convert, he can immediately sit and pray in the front row of the mosque, at the place of worship, near the tomb. He can perform Namaz. Thus, there is an absence of obstacles to his rituals.

Guru: There are other reasons for this position of Islam you mentioned. Likewise, only two great men have been born here. As a result of Hindus twisting and manipulating it, the term Hindu has been debilitated to a state where it cannot command respect. One is Sri Krishna. He was born in the Yadava clan, which can be called a downtrodden section.

It must be determined that at a time when there was no notable capability or skill, a royal family existed on the basis that might is right. The proof of this is that all the children born before Krishna were killed. Yet, through the stories, Vasudeva was highly praised and glorified in later times.

So it must be believed that except for those belonging to that royal lineage, the rest lived as poor people, as Shudras. The proof of this is that there is a group called Krishnavargakar in the Nair community today. They are just poor people. Cattle grazing is their occupation. Seeing them, one feels that they are not leading an extravagant life. Just as how many sections are encompassed within the single word 'Harijan', similarly, when we say Nair, there are several sections within it. Is it not proof that all of them have been divided and marginalized? The term Nair came down and reached even the Vilakkithala Nair. The pot-maker is also called Pillai and Nair. But what benefit has this aforementioned group given to all of them? Likewise, by giving them names like Mooppakkudi and Velakkudi, they have tried to complete their marginalization. Although the membership here appears as a large number when mentioning the name Nair, when it is subdivided, it reaches a state where we ourselves find it hard to believe how it all stands. Thus, many people belonging to this class and caste have gone back here.

Among the Ezhavas of the south, four illams (lineages) are mentioned: Mootillam, Choyillam, Pallichayillam, and Mayyanattillam. Among the Ezhavas of the north, four are mentioned there as well: Thandan, Channar, Ponamban, and Panikkar. Then it spread and became Vaduvar. Looking at it this way, it is impossible to express in words how much of a mockery this is. This is said about those who have earned the name of a prominent community based on numerical strength. Below this, how many countless castes are there. A high standard has been set regarding these two communities, hasn't it? Even these so-called high communities have not been able to play any significant role here.

In recent times, because the Shudras here had the royal rule in their hands, they did slightly better in Kerala; otherwise, Shudras still have no position in North India. While saying that, people of various kinds are lumped together under the designation of Harijan. A new name has been given to it: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe. When it comes to that, the people called Harijans today merely face a disadvantage. All these mentioned groups were lying in such a state. There is no doubt that within the next eighty years, this group will reach the position where all the others are currently standing.

The reason for this is that the government, consciously or unconsciously, in every sector under the name of democracy, has established that education and wealth can belong to everyone, and that a position in the government can belong to anyone. If we look into history, we will understand that the prominent communities here did not have much of an advantage. Isn't it clear that this marginalization occurred because the governments in their respective times viewed people with different perspectives? Similarly, today the government gives equal freedom everywhere to the backward Christians and Harijans. Moreover, it provides all the necessary financial assistance for them. At this rate, if we look back after eighty years, the upcoming eighty years will bring them to the level of those who are called the greatest prominent communities today. There is no doubt. Therefore, in any era, there is no doubt that people will be marginalized or prosper depending on the manner in which the state handles and leads them.

However, due to the magnitude of time or for some other reason, Islam has incurred certain shortcomings. They will do many things to show greatness through their rule. Because of that zeal, the stories most commonly seen in Arabian history are those of imprisoning one's father and ruling by oneself. A proof of this is Pakistan and Bangladesh. Even though the Prophet was accepted as a messenger, there is a history of even his children being murdered. It is not customary to kill the priestly class. Yet, we see it being done. Because of the Prophet's steadfastness, wealth and popularity came to them. Now, they are unable to adapt and practice it properly according to the times. If merely one thousand five hundred years of the Prophet's era have been made like this, we see an inextricable knot when we consider what the countless historical treasures of the Hindus are, which cannot even be fully enumerated.

Therefore, even if the question you asked is correct now, it must be inferred that some children of God would have been born among that group as well to remove their marginalization. We must believe that a great man like Ayyankali is a seed of sacrifice. As a result of it, we can believe that today, even in Kerala itself, there are many children in the government, just like powerful people such as Dr. Ambedkar, Devaraj Urs, and Ram, who were even capable of drafting our constitution. All these are sufficient grounds to dispel our doubts.

That is why I stated that, having progressed correctly for eighty years, God has established a state of affairs here such that no government, whether affiliated with a party or not, can discard any of this. Therefore, there is no room for doubt in this matter. Another point, and the only thing I repeatedly urge caution about, is this. We have a society here where even the ascetic monasteries, established by cunning scholars who deceived people in the name of Sanatana, Advaita, and Hinduism, have not lifted a finger to eradicate its evil practices.

It should not be inferred from this that the intention is to condemn them or to banish them in order to move forward. We must also believe that it is perhaps by divine design that they attained certain positions of status, and that through their cunning intellect, they have been able to control and govern the masses to this day. However, we can affirm with confidence that the wise will not reject this era—an era most conducive for them to unite with all human beings, exercising compassion while remaining steadfast in the philosophical principles of Sanatana. This can be achieved if even these capable and cunning individuals strive to impart cooperation and good sense to others in accordance with the present times, thereby demonstrating the unity of human society. Let us conclude this with a prayer that the greatest good sense may prevail.
Guruvani
September 1981
Birthday Message
Disciple: What prompted you to take up ashram life?
Guru: An inherent inclination that unknowingly existed before merely found an opportunity to manifest itself more clearly, that is all.
Disciple: What was that opportunity?

Guru: It was the ignorance within the household. What I mean by ignorance is—my stepfather, the absence of a father—because of that, we were at the place where my mother was married a second time. There, my stepfather would drink, and quarrels surrounding that were a regular occurrence. This was the cause for the motivation.
Disciple: You considered this as an opportunity?
Guru: Yes, this came as an opportunity.
Disciple: After this opportunity arose, towards what did that initial inclination of yours turn?

Guru: This inclination further sharpened the aspect of devotion. Thus, although the desire for an ashram life was within me for two years, since I was in an environment where I did not know how to go about it, I felt like going to Palani. For that purpose, I undertook vows and walked around with a garland around my neck like others do. After two years passed like this, everyone started asking why I was not going. I replied that I would go when the time comes, and that extending the duration of the vows would not cause any harm.
Disciple: Was it after going to Palani that you reached this state?

Guru: I did not go to Palani. I went to the ashram itself. One day, due to a quarrel with my stepfather, I spent that night in a bhajan mutt there. The next morning, I went to the guru who had taught me the alphabet and requested him to take me and enroll me in some ashram. He fulfilled that desire.
Disciple: In which ashram did he enroll you?
Guru: Initially, it was in Kalady. Since things were not right there, I came straight to Aluva and reached the Aluva Advaita Ashram.
Disciple: What was your age at that time?
Guru: Fourteen years old.
Disciple: At that age, when you raised such a request to him, he took you straight to an ashram without saying anything else, didn't he!
Guru: He already knew more information about me beforehand. It was with this understanding that he did this.
Disciple: His name?
Guru: Kumara Pillai.
Disciple: Whose was the ashram where he first took you?
Guru: Agamananda Swami's - Sri Ramakrishna Mission.
Disciple: Was it with the intention of leading a monastic life that you started the ashram life even then?
Guru: Certainly.
Disciple: In that regard, I have a desire to know about each experiential realm of the life you have had since then, that is, about each experience of the monastic life.

Guru: I came to the Aluva Advaita Ashram and spent two years there. After that, I was invited to Sivagiri. I came to Sivagiri and spent quite some time in the branches of Sivagiri.
