After spending four continuous years in Sivagiri itself, they sent me to various institutions. I also spent a considerable time taking charge of those institutions. Altogether, seventeen years were spent in Sivagiri and its affiliated branches.
Disciple: In spiritual matters, there is a tradition of initiating one into the monastic life, that is, giving spiritual instruction (upadesha). Did you receive that from Sivagiri itself?

Guru: No. There is such a practice in Sivagiri. They usually do it at the time of bestowing the saffron robes. Until then, many live there under the boundary of being a brahmachari. However, I had felt earlier that an instruction devoid of spiritual experience was unnecessary. Therefore, I did not receive instruction from them.
Disciple: You deliberately refrained from receiving it.
Guru: Yes.
Disciple: Then, during which period and from whom did you receive the instruction?

Guru: During my time spent at Sivagiri and its branches, while at Aruvippuram, I developed a strong, indescribable desire to find a guru possessing true experiential merit. While I was pondering how to attain this, a person named Vijayan (from Karinkulam), who was a disciple of a wandering ascetic known as Pathani Swami, spent a night with me. The next morning, saying, "You are quite good, I will show you a Swami," he took me along. We went towards the beach. Reaching the beach, we walked from Vallakkadavu to Poonthura. While returning and arriving amidst the thickets on the western side of Beemapally, he was there.

He did not have the appearance I had imagined. A very large, dark figure. With a very long beard and wide, staring eyes, his physique evoked a formidable disposition. He was wearing a piece of a sack. It was getting close to dusk. Therefore, I did not approach him. When Vijayan went and sat to speak with him, I heard him say in Tamil that he did not know me. Saying "Alright, let it be morning," he let it go. That night, we slept at Beemapally. The next day, very early in the morning, while I was bathing, he came down that way. Seeing me walking like that, he called out and imparted the instruction to me right there and then.
Disciple: You mentioned that you received the instruction; within how much time after that did you have the spiritual experience?
Guru: It was two and a half years after receiving the instruction that this realization occurred. Prior to that, I happened to receive a vision. In a very clear manner.
Disciple: What was thatٹ

Guru: That was—during the time I resided at Aruvippuram, there was an occasion when I was mentally and physically exhausted. The mental exhaustion was partly due to certain difficulties from the administration. Another was the distress of not attaining this, of seeking for the sake of spiritual matters and not attaining it; the body wearing out with daily fever. Waking up at four o'clock every day was a routine. One day when I woke up, I felt dizzy and fell, hitting the wall. It was six o'clock when I managed to get up from there.

That day, there was such an exhaustion of the mind. The body gave out too. And the purpose for which I came was not fulfilled. What would this life be? Thinking like this, I felt that I did not come desiring any of this. If the body goes, let it go. What is there to think more about it? When I felt that way, a sort of courage came over me, and I quickly performed the daily routines. There is a full-length portrait of Narayana Guru Swami in a room of that southern building. After sitting there and performing prayers and pujas, I immediately felt that I should go to the place where he meditated. Going there, I made a firm resolve that day to climb this hill for forty-one days and see what happens, and thus I kept going for forty-one days. On the fortieth day, upon reaching there and looking up from the rock, I suddenly saw a halo, much like the halo of the moon. And within it, a face. That face was unfamiliar to me. Since I was unfamiliar with what it was, a sudden shudder went through my body. And I climbed down.

That evening, I went to Neyyattinkara to fetch oil for the temple. While there, another acquaintance invited me into a coffee shop. As I was drinking coffee, I looked up and saw a portrait of the very figure I had seen earlier. Upon inquiring whose portrait it was, I was told that it was Rishi Sai Baba. I resolved then that if I ever were to build a humble dwelling, I would enshrine this portrait there first.
My experience with my Guru was thus—without my speaking another word, and without his saying anything further, I received his spiritual initiation.
Disciple: I fail to comprehend that. What does it mean to receive initiation without either party exchanging a word?

Guru: The purpose of my visit was stated in a single word. He also posed a question in a few words: 'For what purpose have you come?' I replied, 'For whatever may bring peace to my soul.' These were the only words exchanged. Embracing me with tears, he declared, 'You are the rightful heir.' He then wrote down the initiation. Without uttering another syllable, he instructed, 'Very well, take this and continue to utilize it in this manner.' They were two mantras. 'Within three months of utilizing this mantra, two signs will manifest. They will appear in a dream. You must return here then.' Accordingly, the signs appeared, and I returned. The Guru stated that everything was present, yet there would be a considerable delay. It was only after approximately two and a half years that a continuous series of experiences commenced.
Disciple: Could you perhaps elaborate on those experiences in a manner that we might comprehend?

Guru: Merely recounting the experience to you will not render it comprehensible. This experience entails the manifestation before us of a light or form that we had not anticipated. It must not be a projection of our intentions. That is its underlying truth. If it were anticipated, would it not merely be a materialization aligned with one's own thoughts?
Disciple: Indeed, it would imply that it arose in accordance with one's imagination.

Guru: Is it not correct to say it manifested from his imagination? Did he not possess such an imagination? He certainly did—regarding God,ٹ he will only receive what is conducive to his mental transformation at that particular moment. However, that is not the case. From its primordial form, it must manifest beginning from whatever he initially experienced, in accordance with the evolution of the soul that has been instrumental throughout his successive incarnations.
Disciple: It must emerge from the earliest stage, that is, from the very inception of the soul.

Guru: Affirmative. It must manifest in accordance with the meritorious deeds of the soul's primal incarnation. Therefore, it ought not to manifest in this manner. It should not appear in the form currently venerated, nor in forms that have passed, nor in those anticipated in the future; rather, it dawns within him in accordance with the destiny of that specific incarnation. It is utterly impossible to articulate this in words. One can only rely upon what has been seen and heard.
Disciple: Indeed.

Guru: Consequently, what will you comprehend from this? You shall comprehend nothing. I might claim to have seen Shiva, to have seen Vishnu, to have witnessed myriad other entities, to have beheld the entirety of nature, and to have observed numerous forms that have manifested within nature unto this day. However, none of this will foster any true comprehension. Merely uttering the words jaggery, sugar, clarified butter, and honey, and attempting to taste them—will that yield any sweetness?
Disciple: No.

Guru: Even licking the written words will impart no sweetness. It must be properly cultivated and refined. Such refinement can only be achieved by each individual themselves. It cannot be cultivated through any other means whatsoever.

Disciple: We earnestly desire to hear through which stages and by overcoming what obstacles you have attained your current state, presented in a manner that provides us with an understanding of the unique characteristics inherent to each realm of these experiences.

Guru: As I have previously recounted to you, a form of which I had neither heard nor possessed prior knowledge manifested before me. Prior to that, for seventeen years, I offered worship at the samadhi of Narayana Guru and at the site of his consecration. I derived no such spiritual experience from that practice. That was not what materialized before my vision. If you inquire as to how this occurred, what am I to say? Even if I were to explain, it would invariably appear as a paradox.

Disciple: Indeed, many individuals who visit here genuinely report such experiences. The populace generally perceives it as deeply wondrous when these individuals claim to have beheld Shiva, or to have witnessed other divine forms. Conversely, however, their entire lives frequently appear to be an accumulation of profound sorrows. We are eager to comprehend the underlying reasons and dynamics behind this paradox.

Guru: Let us address that matter. I have stated previously that the deities, ascetics, and sages depicted in our Puranas today, as well as the adherents of the four subsequent paths—namely Karma, Yoga, Jnana, and Bhakti—have manifested in accordance with their past innate tendencies. Nevertheless, they have recorded that they beheld Shiva, or their accounts align with the words conveyed by the authors of the Puranas in accordance with our Hindu Dharma. We have had the occasion to observe this phenomenon here as well. Do we not hear individuals here, ranging from young children to those fifty years of age, claiming to have seen various specific divine figures?
Disciple: Indeed.
Guru: All of this must be witnessed. It is indeed necessary to behold such things. However, it is incongruous with the present era.

Disciple: Thus, you have elucidated the nature of these experiences, noting that they manifest in specific individuals. Yet, following this explanation, you declared that they are unsuited for the current epoch. However, is it not within this very epoch that children and individuals of all ages are experiencing these phenomena?
Guru: Affirmative.
Disciple: What, then, is meant to transpire in this present epoch? What are its defining characteristics? How ought one to approach it? We possess an earnest desire to comprehend this as well.
Guru: The culmination of a Chaturyuga is constituted by four distinct Yugas.
Disciple: So the scriptures decree.

Guru: Herein, we can observe this progression through the lineage of Manu. This framework serves to distinguish the epochs of the deities from those of mankind. The eras dominated by the deities are the Treta Yuga and the Dvapara Yuga. As the Dvapara Yuga approached its twilight, Krishna emerged as the venerable figure who unequivocally demonstrated a more complete manifestation of human liberty. It is evident that upon his advent, Krishna accomplished numerous feats demanding far greater contemplation than those of the deities who had presided up to that juncture.
Disciple: Indeed.
Guru: Among those clearly discernible feats, the most significant pertains to the profound trepidation experienced by Arjuna, and the subsequent eradication of that very fear.
Disciple: Indeed.

Guru: Until then, Arjuna held the belief that the deities, ascetics, and sages as per the scriptures, as well as the associated gurus and uncles who were their followers, were all to be respected. Arjuna had within him something capable of removing all of this in an instant to reveal his inherent nature, yet he remained in a state where he could not understand or act upon it. The merit of a guru lies in correcting this. History says that Arjuna was with Krishna for about fifty years. Yet, it is said that Arjuna still doubted Krishna and questioned him again. Finally, sitting on that battlefield, he asked - "Do you believe me?" "I certainly believe you," said Arjuna. "Then why are you not doing what I say?" "I will not do such things. It is not in accordance with Dharma." - How can one say "I believe you" and "it is not in accordance with Dharma" at the same time? "I certainly believe you. But citing this moral condition, it is not right to kill uncles, others, and gurus. Therefore, I will not do it," he said.

"Let that be, you know me." "I know." "Why did I come? See why you have come now." This means he is speaking of his wisdom. We call it vision (Darshan) here. Arjuna could also receive it, just like these children receive it. Sitting there, he looked. He showed that he had come to reclaim the state of this era. "Alright, do you believe that?" "I believe."

"Alright, then we must see in what all stages we both have taken this human birth since the beginning." He looked - and then within half an hour, he received a detailed understanding of why they had come in all stages, how they had lived together, whether they had a guru-disciple relationship, etc. Only after that did he stand up without questioning, immediately prostrate at his feet, take up his bow and arrows, and kill everyone. This is the incident, isn't it? That is a proof.

Prior to that, no guru who had come until then had ever orchestrated an event in this world where uncles and gurus were killed in this manner. No one other than Krishna was there to prove this as a first step to demonstrate that this is a complete epoch of man. After that, there is a part where Krishna himself says - "Kali has begun. It is no longer our time" - which part is that?
Disciple: It is said that after the war, in connection with the ascension to heaven, it is the period to strive for liberation (Moksha). That is the occasion.
Guru: There was an occasion back then when Arjuna lost in a battle. Which one is that?

Disciple: It is Vyasa who speaks more about that. After Krishna's ascension to heaven, asuras came to Dwaraka and started abducting the women. Arjuna came to protect them. But Arjuna found himself so devoid of strength that he could not even lift his bow and arrows. He had to stand there unable to fight. And the asuras abducted all those women.

On this occasion, when Arjuna prepares to commit suicide with the intention of ending his life, Vyasa advises him. This is now the era to seek liberation. At the beginning of Kali Yuga, the devas (deities) have no power. He says that this happened not because of your incompetence, but because if you use these weapons acquired from them, it is a time when they have no power, and therefore the effect of those mantras has also been lost. He also tells him to strive for liberation.

Guru: Alright, so that is clear to you. The time has come for man to strive for liberation. The Kali Yuga is for humans. It is understood that even if a man becomes a deva, he has no power. So, the meaning is that one must progress from there. What do we get from these words? That the position of a human-god is not enough, isn't it?
Disciple: Yes.

Guru: Even today, we worship deities. Our Puranas have been fabricated in such a way that we worship not only gods and goddesses but even spirits like Madan, and our Vedic scholars taught us to continue the accompanying traditions and exactly what those predecessors showed us. Only they should perform Vaishnava pooja. Another person can perform Shaktheya pooja. Yet another can do Shaiva pooja. Thus, some people mix everything together. If you keep doing things in this manner, where will you achieve anything in this era? These are some matters that you have missed without realizing. That is why it was said that there is no benefit in this during this era. There will be no benefit from the devas.

Disciple: But still, today it is universally practiced with deities, and people believe there are some minor results, and they make some offerings accordingly, don't they? That is the prevailing system of worship today, isn't it?
Guru: Yes, all that will be there. I didn't say it wouldn't be there. But what is the use of this for you, what benefit does your soul get from this?

Disciple: That is correct. People universally know that this is an era where one must strive for liberation. In a way, chanting names (Namasmarana) is enough. It is said that this is the era where chanting names brings liberation. But how will these people, who do not know what liberation is or where to find the paths for it, strive for it today? In this era, whose name will bring liberation? For liberation to be attained through chanting names, liberation is conceived or implied as the soul merging into Brahman, isn't it?
Guru: Yes.
Disciple: So if that is the case, it can be said that the desired subject is purely a spiritual matter.
Guru: Yes.
Disciple: Then, it is not recorded anywhere in the Puranas that anyone received this from the devas anywhere.
Guru: No.
Disciple: Moreover, when the devas themselves were asked about this subject, they too said to seek a Guru for it.
Guru: Yes.
Disciple: So an appropriate Guru is required for that today. Then what is the way for these people to attain this through such a Guru? How should one search for it? Shouldn't there be such a Guru?

Guru: Yes, we have received a notification about that here. That is, through celestial voices (Ashariri) and otherwise. So such words are proof for us. We can take that as a foundation stone. From the time of Krishna, a different nature has emerged. Krishna is the last guru of Dvapara Yuga. In our experience, we received all visions in the nature of Darshan from that Krishna himself, and experienced all the difficulties from this. It is hard to express the difficulty of that experience. In short, all the gods and goddesses, yogis, sages, and ascetics till date appear in their vision and instruct them like this. They will indeed speak the truthful words. After moving forward like this for a while, their words will falter. We won't experience that word.
Disciple: The words spoken by these devas and sages?

Guru: Yes, even we do not know why that is. We searched but could not grasp it. Such experiences happened for about seven and a half years, and various kinds of changes occurred. Each of these deities would come and say something. It would be correct at first. Then it would not be correct. Like that, it changed rapidly. All kinds of sages have come.
Disciple: You mentioned that the preceptors of all religions and all sages have come, haven't you?
Guru: Yes.
Disciple: Will all the great sages come like that?
Guru: They will come.
Disciple: If they come?
Guru: When they come, they give their vision; others will tell some things.
Disciple: The preceptors of all religions - Christ, Prophet, Guru Nanak - won't all those who are mentioned like this come?
Guru: Everyone will come, no one will be left out. Their souls will come and shed tears for this - that is out of joy - and they will instruct us. They will say this by calling out, "Children."
Disciple: It was said that all the religious teachers would come and instruct us. What will they say? What will they ask?

Guru: When these religious teachers arrive, they will display some joy. While displaying that joy, they will ask through the vision they receive, "Do you have anything to give us? Tell us what we should do." Then they themselves will tell us: "You do not have much to gain from us. All of this is already embodied in your Guru. You cannot demand and receive anything from us that is not available from that Guru. We shall impart certain things to you. You must not deviate from them. You only need to follow this specific discipline, without violating that word, the word of the Guru. You will attain everything from it" — this is what was instructed then.

Disciple: If it is stated that all the religious teachers have come and they have nothing specific of their own to offer, and that everything is encompassed within your Guru, it seems this mission is intended for the emergence of a universal religion. What do you have to say regarding this?
Guru: There is no reason to doubt that at all. Because, apart from what these teachers stated, everything we have received since then up to this day has already been proven.
Disciple: One more thing, the teachers who have arrived are individuals who founded respective religions.
Guru: Yes.

Disciple: However, the spiritual teachers who have come to the world are exceedingly numerous. Why is it that, instead of all of them, only a very few individuals are present here in a manner worthy of being mentioned by name?

Guru: That depends on the era. Krishna arrived during a specific epoch. He appeared in the final phase of the third Yuga within a Chaturyuga cycle. A transitional stage where another Yuga was commencing. That is, Krishna appeared on a path that specifically proved through God himself that freedom had been attained by humanity. Following that period, most of those who have subsequently arrived on this path are Gurus themselves; they are referred to in two different terms as either prophets or Gurus. Apart from that, everything is primarily attributed not as being spoken by deities, but entirely by the Gurus. For instance, it was these great sages (Rishis) who discovered and wove the garments we use today, and who formulated the medicines for our treatment when we are afflicted by illness.
Disciple: It is exactly like that.

Guru: That is what can be observed through history. Therefore, it becomes evident that these were imparted to them. Whatever was required for human utilization during this era was received from God. However, they conveyed it while keeping it concealed. That might be due to the magnitude of their erudition or similar factors. It is also possible that they received it with the instruction that it should only be expressed in such a manner. Otherwise, they would not have done so. They have never been questioned as to why they did it this way.

They say that upon seeing a plant, one can ask it, "Who are you?" Or it will proactively say, "I am suitable for this purpose, you may take me for it." Thus, it is clear that such knowledge was divinely communicated to them. Otherwise, how could they extensively document so many medicinal remedies? How did figures like Bhogar's twelve thousand or seven thousand even emerge? It is impossible to merely discover them. By the time one discovers a medicine and determines its exact weight, dosage, and properties, an entire lifetime would pass. This was not the case; the knowledge of these medicines was systematically imparted to them. That is exactly what they have documented. Otherwise, it would have been impossible to compose and compile so many verses (Shlokas). It is acknowledged that Agastya, Bhogar, and several other profound masters received knowledge in this manner. Their traditions continue on that basis.

However, many great souls have appeared even before this to elevate the world to a certain level. As evidence of this, the most significant among the lineage presented to us are the Manus and the lineage of the Manus. But, apart from their names being briefly mentioned in the Puranas, it is not entirely clear what the Manus accomplished. The reason for this lack of clarity is that we have received a revelation here indicating that a mistake occurred on their part in some manner. That mistake is ego (Ahamkara). The reason for this is that today's ascetics (Sannyasins) use a phrase — 'Aham Brahmasmi' — meaning 'I am Brahman'. Today, almost all of us use that Vedantic phrase. We too develop the egoistic notion that everything belongs to the mind, and everything is driven by the mind. Do we not?
Disciple: Yes, we do.

Guru: The scholars state, "O man, it is your mind." If the ego takes possession of that mind, would not this entire state go awry? This originates from the Brahman. I have merely become an instrument for that divine resolve. I have been blessed with a fortune in it. One can receive this only by remaining in the humble realization, "I must bow down and perceive it." Otherwise, apart from repeatedly chanting the absolute phrase "I am Brahman", one will never truly receive the divine words.
Disciple: Yes.

Guru: Among those who are referred to as ascetics, they talk about this wholeness, saying things like it is the great absolute, the nectar of existence-consciousness-bliss (Satchidananda), and so forth. However, it must be understood that they are speaking without having any profound knowledge about it. Because they can only record the words received from the Brahman in a manner suitable for use across different eras. The reason this wisdom resided only in a select few masters like Vasishtha and Vyasa is because they were entirely devoid of ego. It was received exclusively by those who stood without ego, in a state of humble supplication, thinking, 'I do not know anything; whatever is bestowed upon me, I shall faithfully execute.'
Disciple: Has it not been received by those who are otherwise?

Guru: No. Nor can it be obtained merely by speaking. Similarly, from the knowledge we have received, we can understand that in the lineage of the Manus as well, they were afflicted by some form of ego. Thus, all the great souls who have appeared to date must have made some errors at one point or another. It is among the mistakes that occur due to their intellect or their close familiarities. It has happened to everyone. No one can escape without committing that error. After all, they were born as human beings, were they not? Therefore, if they impart words as their own without deeply beseeching for them, such errors will inherently creep in. Hence, not a single word of one's own should be employed in this matter.
Disciple: In this specific matter?

Guru: It must not be used in this matter. One should not display their intellect or power here. If an individual displays anything as their own, then their true self no longer exists. Everything should be submitted with the attitude: 'We shall perform it in accordance with the resolve of the Brahman. Whatever is Your resolve, that alone is sufficient; there is nothing of my own.'
Disciple: Absolute humility.
Guru: Precisely that. Otherwise, if one proclaims 'I am here', then that divine essence is lost. That is exactly what another Vedanta states—
"Whoever keeps asserting 'I, I'—"
"If sought within, it is not many, but becomes One."
At the same time, something else is mentioned in the '*Harinaamakeerthanam*':
"The moment I perceived You, who is One, as two here—"
"The sorrow that arose, alas, cannot be expressed in words!"
"To return to the original state, Your streams of grace—"
Must flow upon me here, Om Namo Narayana."
Only that grace is permissible. Just that single grace. One must merely beseech for it.
Disciple: In that poem too, it is such a supplication.

Guru: What has come is a supplication. It is not in the manner of 'I already have something, just add a little to it' or 'I already know quite a bit'. Nowadays, some people approach Swamis and say, "I have read and understood quite a lot. Yet, I thought it proper to meet you, listen to you, and speak with you." There is nothing wrong in what they say. They possess everything. Then just a little... But such a question is inappropriate. Full realization can be attained from this only if it is handled with absolute humility. Otherwise, it will not come at all. It will halt. They will just say something and leave. This is the reason why not all the great sages attained it. If one approaches it not with complete surrender but with egoistic pride, the subject ends right there. It will then digress into another topic.
Disciple: Didn't Moses, the Prophet, and Christ receive it in this manner through revelation?
Guru: Yes, they were in a state of supplication. Not even a single word was their own.
Disciple: No, it is known as revelation.

Guru: Yes, the Prophet proved it even more strongly. He did not say it; let Him tell me. I shall tell you. Therefore, it is they who truly proved it in recent times. In these one thousand five hundred years, no one else has come to speak a word like what the Prophet said.
Disciple: No.
Guru: What is the proof for that?
Disciple: There are many preceptors who have come in these modern times like Sri Ramakrishna, Vivekananda, and Chattampi Swamikal. None of them received it as a revelation in this manner.
Guru: The proof that they haven't received it as a revelation is evident from their own words, isn't it?
Disciple: Yes.
Guru: Everything they have said are pure, nectar-like words. Have you ever heard them say anywhere, as their own statement, that 'I received such and such, and I am telling it to you'?
Disciple: No, that is not there.

Guru: Then, what we hear and speak are the words of praise sung by others. That is true. There is no objection to that. Their souls are indeed great; they have grown according to their capacities. All that is true. But they have not personally given the guidance saying, 'This specific word was received from God; now you must walk this specific path'. They too are demonstrating to us by walking the path of acknowledging the preceptors who came before.
Disciple: So, from what you are saying, it is understood that some people come specially to accomplish certain things according to God's will.
Guru: Yes.
Disciple: Some come otherwise. They walk through their own spiritual realms like this.
Guru: Yes.
Disciple: It is understood that there are people belonging to such two distinct realms.

Guru: Not two, there are people from many realms. They are all great souls. They all do and make others do things to some extent in accordance with their times. It does not mean they are not Gurus. But they cannot say everything in harmony with this time.
Disciple: Not by God's will.

Guru: No. They must come by God's will. They must come specifically to do that task; only then can they express a conclusive opinion. The histories of Moses, Jesus, and the Prophet are proof of this. I am not saying that others have not received revelations. People who have spoken with such profound revelations are rare.
Disciple: This subject has not been spoken of in this manner.
Guru: Furthermore, this has not happened through me. The Devas and Rishis have also said that you will receive it through your Guru.
Disciple: Yes.

Guru: They too did not say it. They have been told to grasp my very life-force in the subtle realm. Everyone here knows—an occasion when Krishna came and instructed us during that testing phase of two or three weeks here. That Krishna Himself said, 'Now hold on to your Guru; grasp that Guru's form just as you grasped me'—and left. They grasped it that way and tried it. It worked. By trying it that way, I mean, there were numerous diseases here. Initially, Krishna said to do it in a specific manner. When done so, it was cured. Then numerous evil spirits afflicted other people. He instructed to do that too in a specific manner. It was done. Back then, there were fifty to sixty people here every day, at any time. They were watching all this. This was done by these children. What do these little children know? Then they were told to grasp my form.
Disciple: Krishna said?
Guru: Yes. That is how they grasped it. That is what is happening even now.
Disciple: Is it after that the worship rituals and chanting of names began?

Guru: Otherwise, I did not create any of this. This is a very profound subject; it works only if you understand it at this level. I shouldn't insert my logic and intellect into this as if it's my own. It won't work either. It has come exactly in this state. Then, my form itself is instructing from the atmosphere. I am not the one instructing, but my subtle form is—meaning, what a phenomenal process this is!

Disciple: When relating to that subject, when understanding that subject, it was the same with Krishna too. Krishna did not show it to Arjuna in the physical body, did He? They always had contact with the physical body. They had it for years, for fifty years. It was only later that he saw it, wasn't it?
Guru: Yes.
Disciple: So Arjuna too understood it precisely by seeing it in the subtle form in the atmosphere?

Guru: So this is precisely the subject we still need to understand. Thus, when such a preceptor comes, shouldn't we understand that we must grasp his form in the subtle, in the gross, in the effect, and in the cause?

Disciple: So it is being grasped in these four states: subtle, gross, cause, and effect. In all these four states, there is a reason seen to view all Gurus in such a way that the Guru can be perceived in that state.
Guru: Yes.
Disciple: Then what is the reason for that? What is the difference in this?
Guru: As I said. In this fourth state, these Gurus cannot merge in the cause and the effect. It is the state of a Deva. Because they do not create the cause. Nor do they create the effect.
Disciple: The cause is not created by the Deva?
Guru: No. It arises from Brahman. Therefore, only a Mahatma who reaches the state of Brahman can do this.
Disciple: Can it be seen in all these four states?
Guru: Yes. That prophethood can only be created that way. So, only a Mahatma who comes like that can handle this. This special state exists only in him. The scriptures do not speak of such Mahatmas.
Disciple: When grasped in the gross, the subtle, the cause, and the effect, the Guru is seen, isn't he?
Guru: Yes.
Disciple: Does that mean this vision is possible in all spheres of nature and in all animate and inanimate beings?
Guru: Yes.
Disciple: So, what is said to have been experienced, conceiving the Guru as Brahman, falls within the definition described in the language of Vedanta regarding Brahman.
Guru: Yes. It means only such a Guru can do that.
Disciple: Is it not just a concept, but a reality?

Guru: It is a reality. It is not an imagined conceptual form. The Devas and Devis are all conceptual forms. As I said earlier, the Deva and Devi are relevant for their specific eras. That is only up to the position of a Deva.
Disciple: So, it is not possible for a Deva or the people who come during the Deva's era to delve into the two aspects of cause and effect at that time, is it?
Guru: It is not possible. A word from the Guru must come. There have been instances where the Guru specially provided them with guidance during a particular era.
Disciple: Still, isn't it an era where they have authority?
Guru: Yes, the Guru remains seated after leaving it to them to do. Holding the position of the Guru, the Guru remains seated, making them act. That is all the Guru can do then.
Disciple: So, any preceptor striving in that epoch can only reach up to this position of a Deva.
Guru: That is all. It cannot grow beyond that. All these things can be seen. Other than that, nothing can be done. This Kali is the most qualified component.
Disciple: Yes. Something like that was mentioned earlier about the era.

Guru: So, it is man who can respect and understand this era. Those with an elevated mental state, known as humans today, are like deities. It must be believed that even the common people here possess such a high level of intellectual prowess. The reason for this is, haven't you seen the capability of those who invent this science today? By discovering and applying it, they are carrying out a creation of their own.
Disciple: They themselves carry out a creation. Yes, that authority, in a way, seems to have been set aside for man. In the name of logic.

Guru: Thus, merely by using the intellect, one is able to invent something like a deity, in such a way that a creation itself emerges among humans. But it will not cross beyond that. It will not reach reality. Haven't deities also performed great illusions? It has been depicted that they did so during their time. Similarly, in a future era, if it is written that these people are great deities and they did such and such things, what is anyone going to do?
Disciple: It is not surprising either.
Guru: No. They have conducted all of it.
Disciple: In a way, it must be said that they have more capability than a deity.

Guru: But due to the era, a situation has arisen where these gods and goddesses cannot function in the human world today. It has been stated that in this era, man himself must become a deity and the deity must attain liberation. That is the virtue of Kali. Yet, it has been said that this Kali is unacceptable. To whom?
Disciple: To the deity.

Guru: It is unacceptable to the deity. In this era, fools are jumping around without knowing any of this, calling out to gods and goddesses. Today's worship will only yield the result of them worshipping this demon.
Disciple: If Shiva is worshippedٹ
Guru: That is not for the worship of Ishvara.

Disciple: Yes, it does not become Ishvara worship. No, it should not be called Ishvara worship, it is Daiva (God) worship onwards that should be stated. Ishvara is placed at a fourth level. When we say Ishvara, all of these are forms of Ishvara. These are the ones called Ishvaraٹ So, it is about them in the sense of, "O Ishvara, you are thisٹ ". The other one is not like that. What is called Daiva (God) is the most glorious in everything, yes, merged in everything, encompassed in everything, the one.

Guru: What encompasses a little more is called Brahman. What encompasses even a little more than that is called Para Brahman. One must see and understand all these stages. Otherwise, you cannot do anything standing as a mere revelation.
Disciple: However, it is said that man today has the freedom to enter into that realm.

Guru: The reason for saying that man has the freedom to enter into that realm today is that Kali is a state of freedom today. We are seeing today the mixed era that Krishna spoke of. Today, there is hybridization in every aspect. Governance is a mixture, every object we use is a mixture.
Disciple: Yes, and that is the Yugadharma.

Guru: That is the Yugadharma. So, a mixed era has arrived. Shouldn't man also become a mixture? This is the very era described as a mixture where all these mentioned things have come together. Respecting this era, all our modes of worship should proceed accordingly. Now, when saying mixture, it does not mean that the mode of worship should also become a mixture. The mode of worship was already mixed, rising from there and gaining this mental illumination, and rising further, this is the stage of sitting in the nature of an Acharya and imparting that current form according to the resolve of Brahman in a way that is usable by the common people.
Disciple: This era...

Guru: Yes, discarding such an era and talking about some things that passed away somewhere is like what Vaikom Muhammad Basheer wrote, "My grandfather had an elephant." There is nothing more to it than that. Even today is an era of experience that needs to be narrated and known by us. We must understand this era of experience. If these three eras had their respective stages, doesn't the fourth era today have a stage? Doesn't it have its own grandeur and glory?
Disciple: It must have.
Guru: Isn't that glory what is seen today? So, isn't there a duty to inquire and know how to respect this?
Disciple: The people have it.

Guru: If the complete lack of wisdom among those people means they only turn towards whatever, wherever, anyone says, what can be done? Calling it superficial civilization, if they only run after some wealth and the influence of some machines, and merely decorate themselves following some antics, then what is to be done?
Disciple: Nevertheless, due to the Yugadharma itself, it has to undergo a change, doesn't it? Then what is the way for that?

Guru: Will you get it if you sit agape, saying that it will change by itself due to the Yugadharma? Hasn't that Yugadharma been shown? So, hasn't it been proven that you did not go the way you were supposed to go?
Disciple: The people did not go, but even if they didn't, shouldn't the divine resolve happen?

Guru: It shouldn't be called the divine resolve. The resolve of Brahman will come. But you will not see it. Then your era will change. So, shouldn't you practice and understand it with the intellect, capability, and effort with which you lived today? If you say it is difficult now, it is just like there being no wages for one who does no work. If you can do anything about this, it is now that you must act.

Disciple: It was indicated earlier that a mistake was made regarding Manu. Because of that, things have come to be this way today, and it was said that some matters concerning Manus in the past were mentioned in the Bhagavatam, but a detailed and accurate description has not been given. It is seen in the Puranas and Vedas that fourteen Manus have been appointed for fourteen Manvantaras. However, their complete form cannot be known. Yet, it is said that a mistake occurred in these. What it is has not been mentioned anywhere else either. Hearing it now for the first time. There is a desire to know why, and what it is.

Guru: If said now, it is difficult to believe completely. However, since it was received, we have no hesitation in stating it. After all, this is not something we created. Therefore, let us explain. One could say that these Manus and their lineage are completely the cause and effect of the creation of this world. Their path of knowledge is that profound. They have left behind writings about what is needed in the world and how it will be for all time. Thus, their mode of behavior is such that they can be considered the creators and sustainers. If the era of seven such Manus came to be in that manner, wouldn't the actions they performed and their gross, subtle, causal, and effectual aspects be the only things visible? Hasn't action manifested through them? Therefore, they are entirely it.
Disciple: Yes, the manifestation and execution of the actions of each of those can only be seen through them.

Guru: So, when speaking of one Manu among them - a Manvantara consists of seventy-one Chatur Yugas. Do we get an opportunity to think beyond a Manvantara that has functioned for seventy-one Chatur Yugas, rather than just contemplating it? No. After nine such Manvantaras have passed, can anyone think beyond that? Or even if they think, will they grasp it?
Disciple: No, it is not humanly possible.

Guru: Then, when six such Manvantaras had passed, a wise person belonging to the lineage of a Manu sat and pondered thus, realizing that all Manus dissolve in this Brahman. They exist as Brahman itself. Looking within myself, I see them too. They are seen in all moving and non-moving beings. Therefore, I dwell in Brahman, and Brahman dwells in me. Hence, they began to utter "Aham Brahmasmi" (I am Brahman).
Disciple: Is that how these four Mahavakyas came about, the ones like Tat Tvam Asi, Aham Brahmasmi, and so forth?
Guru: Yes.
Disciple: Did these words emerge through an unknown, unconscious impulse?

Guru: We regard this very highly here. It is these four statements that ascetics impart today for renunciation. Thus, when knowing all this, man, overcome by ego, sees himself in everything. When he says he sees everything within himself, won't he become arrogant?
Disciple: Certainly.

Guru: But what is it like? It is like seeing in a mirror. If asked whether anything gets imprinted on the mirror, the answer is no. But this understanding slips away at that moment. These are the mistakes that have occurred. The message given is that this is where the error happened. Therefore, the ego of 'I' is not needed. There is also a saying: 'May this not be felt here, and if it is felt, may it be felt as though all this is me.' Aren't all these words proof for you? So, you can know this without even asking me, if you think clearly.

Disciple: Yes. That is true. Even so, sannyasa initiation is still taking place in India today by imparting Mahavakyas like Tat Tvam Asi. Now, isn't it merely a criterion to be read and understood? Therefore, the knowledge gained through it is only that much. You mentioned a mistake occurred; in which parts did that happen?

Guru: I only have to say the things that were told to me. There is nothing of my own. I can only say here what has been imparted through that command power. There is nothing else of mine to say. That is, when such arrogance arose in the lineage of these Manus, mankind later had to act in a way that their traditional memory itself faded away. The information we received is that they lay exhausted like this for three Chatur Yugas without anything. We have been able to see whether it is right or wrong. But how can it be shown to people like you? You must work it out and see for yourself.
Disciple: Yes. Six Chatur Yugas passed.

Guru: Again in the seventh Chatur Yuga, a creation was given! It was the Trimurti system. It came and completed it within the Chatur Yuga. The subsequent Chatur Yugas will not cross over there. None of them will leave the heavenly realm (Swargaloka). Swargaloka is a realm of virtue where, having attained subtlety, anything can be done anywhere. It can also be seen there in a manner that could be called mere worldly activity. That is what is called a Deva. Again, they will return to the position referred to as 'ksheene punye martyalokam vishanti' (entering the mortal world upon the depletion of merit).
Disciple: Can only the Devas themselves come as humans, approach this Guru, and deal with this very subject before moving on?

Guru: Certainly, there is no doubt about that. Because they do not know such subjects, today's people ask, 'Hey, worshipping a human? What kind of practice is this? Is there such a worship?' Even if you examine the Puranas, Vedas, and Upanishads, this is exactly what is said. You need not worship me. Approaching the Guru is the only way. Thus, all the Puranas have stated that such Gurus are given significance. All the great souls of today have the same thing to say. Then what doubt do we have? There is absolutely no need to doubt.

Disciple: It is indeed so in that matter. However, this mistake that happened to the Manus in these Manvantaras came for twenty-five Chatur Yugas. According to the calculation of the Bhagavatam, it is the twenty-eighth Chatur Yuga. So, after twenty-five Chatur Yugas, three Chatur Yugas have again been lying like this. The era of Vaivasvata Manu. Therefore, within this, numbers like three and ten specifically indicate a time period. The mistake occurred in the third Chatur Yuga. After that, three Chatur Yugas lay idle. In the seventh, the Trimurtis were brought in. It goes like this, doesn't it?
Guru: Yes, exactly like that.
Disciple: So it came like that, returned to twenty-five, and again three Chatur Yugas lay like that. So what about these three and seven?
Guru: It returned again in the third.
Disciple: The other came in a state of completely correcting the mistake. So, is there any special significance to the numbers like three, seven, and ten corresponding to the periods?

Guru: Yes. Isn't this itself the significance? We can see and know all this in the state where it is shown and explained to us. That itself is the clear evidence. We are indeed seeing from Brahman. Thus, when this twenty-eighth Chatur Yuga arrived, it has come back to correction. This is what was explained to us. It is said that many Gurus have come in this Chatur Yuga itself according to the resolve of Brahman. Due to the mistake of these Manus, they too used supernatural powers and other things, went the way of the Devas, and went astray. That deviation is what led to the creation of acharyas again. An example of this is the time of Moses, Jesus, and the Prophet. They have conveyed the very words they received. "This is not mine. This is the Father's. You must accept it." Though the people lacked the knowledge to accept it, they were able to. Because your Puranas continuously spoke of Advaita and merely incorporated it into the poet's imagination, you were unable to reach anywhere. This is its condition.

Disciple: That is correct. Even if we look historically, we have a history before us where the one who worshipped Mahalakshmi became poor, the one who worshipped the goddess of learning ended up uneducated, and yet, after holding a wooden cross, they ruled the entire world and acquired all knowledge and wealth. Therefore, it is at least possible to clearly conceive in this manner that a significant error has occurred. However, it is not possible to comprehend its other aspects through experiential realms.

Guru: The evidence we have here now is that I am not the one who says things here. Innocent young children who have no knowledge and some people who cannot even recognize what this is about are the ones seeing, hearing, and knowing all this. I am merely a medium. I have been presented like this as a medium. This body will perish. But they have already proven that it exists in the subtle form. It is also proven that the subtle is perfect. That is your greatest proof. You will not get a greater proof than this. This is also clear.
Disciple: So, considering all this, I have a desire for you to give the instruction, the message, that you can impart to this world today in the simplest manner.

Guru: What I have to say are the very words that have been revealed to me. It is that such and such a thing will happen after this much time. It has also been revealed that if people do not act accordingly, such and such behavior, situations, and mistakes will occur. Therefore, a solution to that also needs to be mentioned. Today is the Kali Yuga. It has become clear whom we should worship in this Kali. For that, choose an Acharya (preceptor). What kind of an Acharya should come for this? That too was stated clearly. Follow the words of that Acharya. That is the knowledge obtained by grasping the subtle. That is what is going to be distributed through you. That is indeed the divine decree (Brahmanischayam). There is no doubt about it.
Disciple: The first message is that an era has come for people to acquire knowledge in accordance with the divine decree.
Guru: One should realize and understand that it has reached its complete form, and should understand and reject the things seen today.
Disciple: Yes, that is the nature of knowledge.

Guru: So, after taking and understanding a behavior that exists today and that has passed yesterday, and understanding that this is the behavior that should come for tomorrow, to act upon it by assuming the nature of an Acharya today and observing it diligently is what a Guru has to impart. Therefore, one must know about the three periods of time (past, present, and future). Only then can an Acharya instruct it in a way that it can be sustained. This is the way it is told.
Disciple: Is the call to the people to seek a Guru who is a 'Trikalajnan' (knower of the three periods of time)?

Guru: Yes. Only they can say this. So, according to the message we have received about this, let me say a few words. It is said that in the situations according to this divine decree, such and such things will happen in such and such periods. That is a notification. We keep waiting in such a way that this notification can be revealed today. This cannot come completely while I am present, as long as this life is in this body. Why? It is a period where people face quite some humiliation and shortcomings. But, after I am gone, you just need to take all these words and give them out. Anyone whose nose points downwards (meaning ordinary humans) will agree to it. Those whose noses point upwards do not have to agree. There is no need for any doubt.
Guruvani
October 1981
Disciple: What medium do you suggest to stop those who are running today in the name of modernism?

Guru: What is needed is not to stop them. A situation will arise where both the one who runs and the one who makes them run will stop running. There is a proverb that the leg pain is the same for the one who runs and the one who chases. He made the other run because he had more health. The other is running to escape from death. This one's is the frantic run of arrogance. Due to excessive panting, this one will also become like the other. The knowledge given by God that certain things will happen in the world is here. If this is the period when we got the notification, religious scholars and prophets celebrate that great souls have said this even before this. Jesus and the Prophet have indicated this in various parts in the culture of Sanatana.
Disciple: I wish to hear a brief description of what that is.

Guru: What you describe as modern includes machinery, war equipment, and rocket launches discovered through science, right? Very soon, within twenty-five years, some minor untoward incidents will occur in India itself in a way that it will come to a halt. Along with that, there will be numerous opinions and opportunities to carefully study whether this is needed or not. The notification also indicates that a stage might come where India will abandon this along with that. Even if it doesn't happen then, if it is delayed a bit, within three hundred and fifty years, an experi
*Continued from the previous issue

ence will happen to the entire world. At that time, what is called science will become the most hated thing. However, since it was India that discovered this, it should also be the first to disappear in India itself.
Disciple: Why do you say that India discovered this? Wasn't it the Westerners who discovered all this?

Guru: No. Take aeronautics itself as an example. It was a sage named Bharadwaja who wrote it. But when this was discovered, the reason for proving that its capability is very huge is that today we have only one thing to say - that glass which does not break even if hit by arrows or bullets was fitted in the Pushpaka Vimana. Ignoring the Guru's command that no matter what this is here, it will lead to unwanted destruction, that disciple went to Lanka with the stubbornness that he would implement it somewhere. It was created there. Then he reached India with it. He also abducted a girl who was in India. History says that because of that, India suffered disgrace, and the country called Lanka became very degraded and its regime was destroyed.

However, a truth has been revealed in this meanwhile. People do not understand it in that way. This was not done for that woman. Because only if she is abducted, the strength can be known. It was to show that. Proof of this is the history that she was kept in the most special places beautifully and purely without being insulted in any way, and Mandodari herself was particular about keeping her so. From this, if we observe carefully, we can understand that it was not the enmity between kings, but to show the power of this Pushpaka Vimana technology, it was a fight between a guru and a disciple. To show the magnitude and weight of the knowledge, another king was caught. He was astonished to see this. When that happened, destruction became its by-product. Therefore, isn't it clear that this was invented in India itself and that India faced a nature of its destruction even back then? With this much evidence, it would not be correct to say that Westerners invented all this. It is true that we did not venture into any of this later due to the destruction of those times. Thus, after ages and epochs passed, this fell into the hands of a foreigner who arrived here. They translated it into their language and gave it back to the world as their own. Evidence for this are the then universities in India such as Nalanda and Takshashila. While it still stands as evidence today, it cannot be said that the Westerners invented this. The present science - worldٹ indications are that within twenty-five years, the destruction caused by this is likely to happen in other countries even more than in India. Muslims are a group that shows nobility religiously, racially, and administratively. One reason is that they will not let others into their administration and religious solidarity for good or bad. Therefore, infighting occurred among them. It can be seen that some countries will move forward for some more time, create conflicts, and step aside. Similarly, within thirty years in India, some prominent political figures and people of sattvic nature will join together and raise a flag of peace. As if in its shade, two great men will come forward with idealism in the Arabian countries. To accept and act upon it, giving it existence and giving its value and position so as to achieve it, two children are being born in the Arabian countries at this opportunity. They will replicate there the perfect form of peace seen in India then. Similarly, in Western countries, there will be clashes between powerful nations and otherwise. Likewise, communist countries will split into two and fight fiercely. They will face destruction from foreign countries as well. When that happens, not only will all countries fight each other, but the desire for peace will also grow similarly. Then it will be India that has to come to the forefront for that. Because it was India that invented all this. Therefore, even during its time of destruction, India itself will have to come forward and act.
Disciple: Does India or you yourself have any suggestions or concepts to give regarding this?
Guru: Yes. One of them is happening here now. The Akhandanama conducted as per the notification.

The notification that some great souls are being born in this continent for peace - it has not been clearly obtained where. The message is that it will originate within three months. It could be in any corner of the world. But to the God who gave us an opportunity to struggle mentally and physically for that, not just the children of India, but all the children of the world should be happy, and by continuously praying for giving us such an opportunity, we must achieve fulfillment.
Disciple: What is required to attain such a capability?

Guru: For that, all of us believers, without any distinction of class or religion, and without being entangled in the evils of the Varna-Ashrama Dharma seen today, must unite as intelligent children, standing shoulder to shoulder, and raise a national organization imbued with true devotion to God and humility. Through this, the intellect and strength of the people will become even more vigorous and resolute. Today, the community in India that is most appropriately positioned, combining intellect, ability, capability, and shrewdness, belongs to the Brahmin class. Discarding the Varna-Ashrama Dharma, which is their foundation stone, a stone suitable for the era of mixture described by the author of the Gita as Kali Yuga must be firmly established there. They must be able to build a complete society devoid of class or caste distinctions by standing united with others. Otherwise, they must not wallow in the class distinctions seen today. First, step away from the system where there is a special form of worship for them and another for the rest. Instead of anchoring everyone in the Tantric practices seen today, anchor them in true worship of God. Alongside them, who employ all their intellect and ability for this purpose, hold the hands of others and lift them up to the forefront. If they are unable to do this, ideal individuals will emerge from among other classes and implement it. No one will be able to stop them. Then, others will drain away all the assets they have built up, and they will have to suffer the consequences of the power of sin. It would be best if they could collectively undertake both the good and bad deeds they have committed.

Disciple: Based on what you have said, as an intimation received through divine will, shouldn't we consider that God has blessed this to become a lineage of Gurus, established at an appropriate time in the divine conceptualization, much like what was appointed for various eras in the past?
Guru: Yes, I have no doubt about that. That is exactly why I repeatedly and emphatically stated this in everything I said earlier.

Disciple: Is it because of such certainty that you have said many times—"This came without my knowledge; I did not expect to receive this much; I have done absolutely nothing for this, nor have I done anything within this framework"?

Guru: Yes, exactly. To bestow this upon me—someone with no education, wealth, or enlightenment, possessing not even a shred of knowledge—is, in my understanding, akin to the manifestation of fertile natural beauty in the parched soil at the very peak of a desert. This is similar to the word received by Moses in recent times, the revelation received by the Prophet, and the enlightenment received by Buddha. There is no need to doubt it. When we look at their sufferings and their times, we realize how much sacrifice they made. We can see that they even sacrificed their bodies for it.
Disciple: Is that why you say that what contemporaries have said and done is insufficient, and considering its magnitude, what we have experienced is extremely minuscule?

Guru: Yes, that is precisely the reason. Consider how much suffering there was during the time of Jesus. After that, people who believed in Jesus were rounded up every three to six months, tied to whipping posts, beaten, and tortured in various ways, before being thrown bound into lion enclosures, where the contemporaries of that great soul found amusement in watching them being torn apart and having their blood drunk, urging the spectators to cheer. It was only after this went on for twenty-one years that some form of permission was obtained from the government. Similarly, the Prophet was whipped, chased with brooms, and exiled from his country. Look at the miseries Buddha had to endure despite being a prince! The scene where Dayananda Saraswati was even pelted with sandals. Even the experiences Narayana Guru faced recently, or for that matter, the fate Mahatma Gandhi met immediately after a prayer meeting as a result of his efforts to unite a society. When we look at all these without exception and compare them with the ideals we have received, absolutely nothing has happened to us. A certain degree of ignorance among contemporaries is a common occurrence at all times. It is enough to understand ours as the most minor among them. You only have the challenge of cultivating the habit of knowing and imparting this knowledge. Be prepared to secure all kinds of blessings from God for this purpose. That shall be your duty.
Guruvani
November 1981
Disciple: How would it be appropriate if the very people who have thus far displayed intellectual cunning and troubled humanity in every way come to the forefront of this?

Guru: They themselves must come. They are the ones who must accomplish and settle this. This is because, in India, it appears as though all the negative consequences of their various actions over a long period have accumulated, and the burden of sin has rebounded upon them. Therefore, the qualification for this belongs entirely to them.
Disciple: Wouldn't it be better for this to materialize if Christians and Muslims take it up?

Guru: It is good for it to materialize. However, there are some other shortcomings in that. It is a religion that has operated under a single prophet. It does not possess a very long history; it only dates back to the time of Moses. Furthermore, another offshoot called Islam has branched out from it. Both these religions have more or less accomplished what they could from their respective paths. Regarding India, this is even more significant. Through the British administration, they brought order and discipline to humans who had been reduced to a cruel, animal-like state due to the evils of the Varna-Ashrama Dharma; they systematized these poor people by first providing them with something to ensure nutritional sustenance. Similarly, they introduced an enlightened education system. As at least some of these poor people managed to attain it, certain religious and educational institutions rose here with British assistance, resulting in a situation where the administration itself empowered them to outmaneuver these cunning individuals.

The Muslims are not like that. They merely handled a religious system. And then, applied some brute force. They too managed to secure a certain hold in this manner. Even though they secured such a hold, the majority of them are not people who maintain a good status. The reason for this is that they are individuals uplifted from various communities that were culturally deeply degraded. Therefore, no matter how enlightened they become through education and wealth, or how long they are seasoned in administration, they have not reached the path of Sanatana Dharma—an enlightened state combining orderliness, cleanliness aligned with Hindu Dharma, and a pure lifestyle blended with humility. The reason for this is the flaw that occurred when all the aforementioned communities merged and adhered to different religious systems.
Disciple: Is that why they are at the forefront in activities like poultry and goat rearing?
Guru: It is not only because of that, although it can be cited as one reason. It is also due to the advice from those who guide them in ways that foster their economic prosperity.
Disciple: Quite a few such things are happening among us as well, aren't they?

Guru: Yes. Seeing this, some things might have been done. However, that is not at the forefront. What is called Sanatana includes stories that have been passed down from ancient times to the stories up to the author of the Gita existing today. Putting all this together, one only sees a haste to establish Advaita. It is just words. There is no systematization in practice. One who sticks to the character of this Advaita, one who preaches this Vedanta - is so wretched that he cannot even treat his next-door neighbors or his own siblings with equality. That is why it is said that he cannot correct himself from this path. As for Muslims and Christians doing it, their time has only just arrived. Even that resulted in them fighting among themselves and causing various kinds of destruction. Thus, the time has not yet come for them to reach their own peace and survival. Not only that, according to the divine will regarding the era of Manu called Sanatana, it is difficult to find in the history of the world until today any other lineage with such deep reach, such a long-standing history of activity, or a religion that has discovered such a great culture. What is even more important is that the Hindu dharma has the responsibility to guide the lineage of this Manu to function and settle things in the remaining time. The Manu lineage is meant to provide divine dharma to the world. Therefore, the philosophical discipline that encompasses all these world religions is hidden within this. Similarly, it is not easy for the world to bring about another one like it. Thus, attention must be paid to bringing about a complete culture according to the divine will. Whether Christian or Muslim, all religions need to bring this into focus. Even though there is a realization that the complete culture encompassing all religions is one and the same, for each of them, many great people have come and enlightened them with the sacrifices of their respective times and the actions that embodied those sacrifices. Age, experience, etc., have built up many cultures. One can see that uniqueness piled up here and there in the Hindu dharma. It is doubtful whether other religions possess such a great value. To bring about a special character suited to this Kali Yuga by combining what is in other religions as well, all religious followers and all religious scholars must unite and evaluate the hybrid era of the author of the Gita. It is a path that must be completed harmoniously by those living today and those yet to come.

Disciple: Is it in the sense of 'what is to come' that you inform us by saying certain things involving the twelve zodiac signs, nine planets, and twenty-seven stars, and make us understand a method that demonstrates that practical nature?

Guru: Yes. Unless a path of action is implemented by evaluating these three periods, it is not possible to see unity in any other way or to experience in the future the actions done for the good of human society. For this, evaluating the cause, effect, macro, and micro aspects, removing its flaws to that extent can only become possible for our survival, which we preserved earlier, if it reaches up to four or five generations as a systematic progression of a lineage. The summary of the above is that it will not be possible for anyone other than the children who come by the grace of God.

Disciple: Does this mean that all the religious cultures and administrative cultures that have come down through the ages until today should blend together as one, and its own path of practice should come forward as the core, form, fulfillment, and action in the value of human sacrifice?

Guru: Yes. We must certainly understand that only if it happens this way can human effort be evaluated in submission to the divine will, value be assigned to the sacrifice that operates and culminates through it, and the peace and harmony of all of us who worked together in its goodness be realized. I conclude with a prayer that the divine resolve (Brahman's will) may bless us for this.
Guruvani
December 1981
Disciple: Kerala politics, or Indian politics, or world politics - do you have anything to say about this?
Guru: Isn't this what has been said in general - about human life?
Disciple: That was just mentioned briefly in passing, wasn't it? I only asked to clear my doubts.
Guru: What do you mean by clearing doubts?
Disciple: There is an instance here where some politicians, by establishing their rule, even gave gratuity to toddy tappers.

Guru: In a way, one can only say that it is correct. Looking at the current situation, is it worse than current politics? It is just that toddy tappers were paid wages for the work they did. Isn't candidate selection based on caste happening all over India? Then, is giving gratuity to toddy tappers a trick? Toddy tapping, distilling, and drinking have been prohibited fields since ancient times, which subjugate the community.
Disciple: Did you say it subjugates the community in the name of the profession, or about its characteristic effects?

Guru: The characteristics are indeed good. It is just that a habit of handling everything excessively has emerged. Does anyone respect the words of a drunkard? Does he himself know how to respect his own words? Then how will others respect them? Similarly, won't the one who makes and serves it also be included in that? Such people certainly cannot think about the consequences or make a decision and implement it after thinking. If he also gets a gratuity, will he be able to study and improve in this world? What will happen to his children? It is certain that his children will never study. Thus, the intention will complete the old ways too. The trick is that what is older than the old has been completed. Then, we must believe that what is thought of as politics existed here for some time. There is a memory that the light of the predominance of its sacrifice began to be seen from 1944 to 1948. After that, it continued until about 1960 in the name of that weight. I am not saying that some minor things did not happen in between. They have happened.
Disciple: What do you mean by minor things?

Guru: This is just like the proverb that there is no one who would not lick their fingers if they dip their hand into a pot of jaggery. It could be for status, prestige, or making money in any form. Be that as it may! What does that matter to us? What we need is to understand what endures among the people currently involved in all these things, and how they should be able to endure in the future. We must provide an opportunity for the people who are thoroughly disillusioned by seeing all this to think and learn completely. What we need now is to lovingly bring about a sense of unity regarding everything among the people, as mentioned earlier. However, unity in love can only be brought about through a certain kind of fear. Cultivate that fear as if it were towards God, a father, or a mother. Cultivate love and respect. Regardless of what the children of Bharat are involved in, attempt to create a way of life, at least in Bharat, that serves as a model for the world. Through that, the people of the world will desire it themselves. It is not necessary to have a model similar to Russia's in Bharat. Since the situation has not deteriorated to that extent, and since it is not a developed country like America, those methods are not suitable here. The aspect known as India's socialism can only be implemented in one way today. If today's castes or religions can create various political groups, the believers here who think, learn, and teach should stand together to form a national organization, recognizing that believers are one, irrespective of religion and caste. Religious leaders should not be included in this. They should only provide guidance. As Mahatmaji said, one should not desire to cling to it, but merely achieve the objective. Thus, when believers also become those who fear out of love, they will have to respect each other through mutual love. We cannot sustain anything without such love and respect. It seems that on Indian soil, the concept of love is used like a gas. An example of this is communists going out at night to create problems. If a wife and children go to the temple together and someone questions it, they say it was done for their sake. This might be done because they cannot entirely deny a matter that is deeply ingrained in the people. It should be exactly like that. Otherwise, the dynamic between the capitalist and the worker, as well as the attitude of posing as a leader, will inadvertently change. Only then can we believe that there is a government truly belonging to India.
Disciple: Are you certain that such a thing will happen?

Guru: Yes, certainly. It will undoubtedly happen. It is beyond doubt that Bharat will thus become a model for the world. A small proof of this is the emergence of hippies. Even though India is in such a chaotic state, Bharat is still called a spiritual nation. Therefore, wishing that it may happen to the world as the resolve of Brahman, let us conclude this by praying to God.

Disciple: So, based on what we have heard from you, do you have anything further to inform us regarding any doubtful aspects of this solar system, which consists of nine planets, twelve zodiac signs, and twenty-seven stars?

Guru: Yes. As mentioned earlier, this is the era of the seventh Manu. This means that half the time since the origin of the world has passed. It has yet to function for another half of its time. We must believe that there are an unknown number of solar systems in this universe.
Disciple: Do you have any absolute proof for that?

Guru: Yes. One hundred and four solar systems have been observed. Ours is a medium-sized solar system among them. There are stellar constellations seen between them. These stellar spheres are realms where the aforementioned virtuous souls reside. Divine creation has endowed each solar system with a unique nature.
Disciple: Do you believe that any other solar system is more powerful than this one?

Guru: There are numerous other solar systems of greater size and special power. It cannot be said that they are exactly like this one. There are also solar systems with entirely different characteristics compared to this one. Everything in nature undergoes change. A cluster of ten solar systems forms one measurement unit. Thus, there are many stellar spheres that control the existence of the solar system. Those stellar spheres observe and sustain all of this.
Disciple: Why did you say that?

Guru: Just as there is a gravitational field of attraction between this earth and the solar system, there is an attractive force between these stars as well. Accordingly, based on the virtues and sins of a particular solar system, each sphere within the solar system may draw closer to another, or to a stellar sphere.
Disciple: What could be the reason for such drawing closer?

Guru: I mentioned earlier that a human being has only two things to do once born in this world: virtuous deeds and sinful deeds. The result of the sinful or virtuous forces we accumulate as we are born, die, and exist in this world—as its weight increases, it may draw closer to the solar sphere or any other sphere for either destruction or survival. If that drawing closer leads to destruction, fire might erupt due to air pressure itself, causing it to melt and collapse. Alternatively, extreme cold might arise, leading to a state where nothing can survive. Or, everything could be entirely upended, resulting in either complete destruction or partial survival. Conversely, if it draws closer to a stellar sphere that has accumulated virtues, it might cause some destruction but then function in a good state again.
Disciple: In that case, can we know or guess whether it is a region that has committed sins?

Guru: Virtue and sin are not what we merely intend them to be. They are the experiences that befall us if we do not act according to the righteous order ordained by Brahman. We should not assume that we possess the knowledge to understand this and act accordingly.
Disciple: If so, then how do we distinguish between good and bad?

Guru: God has given us a medium to distinguish them. That is the Manus who have passed before us and their lineage. We can only accomplish our actions in accordance with that. If we fail to act accordingly, such things may happen.
Disciple: In that case, if a celestial body undergoes any destruction, will it cause the destruction of this solar system itself?

Guru: No. That will not happen. It may be destroyed or grow due to the pressure of air, water, or other solid substances. Only its physical form will change; its ethereal nature cannot be altered. The change in that ethereal nature occurs just as the specific eras of each Manu change.
Disciple: Are you saying that this solar system will undergo a change only after the era of the Manus is completely over?

Guru: Yes, it is precisely so. Only at such a time will a change occur to it. Otherwise, the calculations would have to be radically altered, not just from this world, but from many worlds. Therefore, God will not do such a thing.
Disciple: So, you mentioned earlier that there are some spheres that are more powerful than this, right?
Guru: Yes, there are. There are certain spheres capable of magnetically attracting not just our actions, but our very earth itself.
Disciple: In that case, a situation could arise where the earth is destroyed or something else happens to it.
Guru: Didn't I mention earlier that it will happen?
Disciple: According to what you said, that happens as a result of sins, doesn't it?
Guru: We must believe so. Only then can we do good deeds and inspire others to do them. Shouldn't we inspire good deeds to the extent of our capacity or knowledge?
Disciple: Should we understand from your words that an earthly nature known in this manner will emerge?

Guru: Yes, that is exactly how it must be understood. Because, according to the calculation believed to be the era of the Manus, only the time of seven Manus has passed. If we have been able to acquire this much knowledge during the time of seven Manus, how much more must be acquired during the era of the next seven Manus.
Disciple: In that case, shouldn't we realize that, based on our knowledge of virtues and sins, we must prioritize virtue?
Guru: Absolutely.
Disciple: But the people today do not seem to understand this and act accordingly, do they?

Guru: Never mind. People will function on their own. If we examine the knowledge that emerged in Russia recently and compare it with the knowledge from fifty years ago, we can discern whether they have progressed or regressed. Similarly, other communist nations, wealthy countries among the Eastern nations, and various other countries within our own Asia have not declined in terms of knowledge; rather, they have ascended.

We know that each of these nations is experiencing a certain anxiety, unsure of what to do as various changes have occurred everywhere. When this anxiety turns into restlessness, humanity will naturally reach a state where it begins to contemplate what must be done. The divine will shall ensure that this happens. If a feeling arises that things are not proceeding according to the cosmic will, and a disturbance occurs in nature, they will all cry out and rectify themselves.

That is the only extent to which their discoveries can survive. Therefore, we must live and act with a firm resolve that everything should unfold according to the cosmic will. Let us pray that all of humanity realizes this.
Guru Vani
